definition_zh: 珍贵的；宝贵的；贵重的；值钱的；娇贵做作的；（precious little）少得可怜
definition_en: worth a great deal because of rarity, love or beauty; costly in material terms; over-refined in manner; and used before little or few to mean almost none
core_image: 掌心托着一枚旧顶针，金属已被磨得发亮
scene: 老人从抽屉最里层取出一只用手帕包着的小盒，盒里躺着一枚褪色的顶针。She never wore the ring because it was too precious to risk losing.
sceneCN: 这里 precious 指「珍贵得不敢轻易动用」（第 1 个义项：因情感或稀有而宝贵）；句意为她从不戴那枚戒指，因为太珍贵，怕弄丢。图中可辨识物件：抽屉深处的手帕、褪色的顶针、磨亮的金属。

pos.zh: 珍贵的；宝贵的；贵重的；娇贵做作的

derivatives.zh: 由 precious 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「珍贵地；做作地」
由 precious 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「珍贵；矫饰」
由前缀 semi-（半）与 precious 复合而成，义为「半宝石的」

senses.title: Worth a great deal to someone
senses.definition: worth a great deal because it is rare, loved or impossible to replace
senses.definitionCN: 因稀有、被珍爱或无法替代而具有很大价值
senses.example: Her grandmother's letters are the most precious thing she owns.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母的信是她最珍视的东西。
senses.why: The Latin noun pretium named the value set on a thing, and its adjective pretiosus described whatever carried that value; English kept the worth and let the money side go.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 pretium 本指给一件东西定下的价值，形容词 pretiosus 就用来形容带着这份价值的东西；英语留下「价值」这一面，把「价钱」那一面让给了 price。

senses.title: Costly because of the material
senses.definition: made of a material that costs a lot, such as gold, silver or a fine stone
senses.definitionCN: 由金、银或上等宝石等昂贵材料制成
senses.example: The crown is set with precious stones brought from the east.
senses.exampleCN: 这顶王冠镶着从东方运来的宝石。
senses.why: A second step inside the same root: pretium also meant the money a thing costs, so the adjective could describe objects whose material alone makes them expensive, not only things loved for memory.
senses.whyCN: 同一词根的第二步：pretium 也能指一件东西所值的钱，于是这个形容词可以形容单凭材料就昂贵的物件，而不只是因回忆而被珍爱的东西。

senses.title: Over-refined in manner or style
senses.definition: too delicate, refined or fussy in behaviour, taste or style, so that it seems affected
senses.definitionCN: 举止、品味或风格过于精细挑剔，显得做作
senses.example: He has a precious way of holding his cup that amuses his friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他端杯子的样子讲究得有点做作，朋友们都拿这个打趣。
senses.why: Value set too high turns into a criticism: a person who treats small things as treasures is called precious in a mocking tone, so the word moves from the object to the attitude.
senses.whyCN: 把价值定得太高就会变成批评：一个把小事情当宝贝的人，会被带着讥讽地叫作 precious，词义于是从「物件」转到「态度」。

senses.title: Almost none, in precious little and precious few
senses.titleCN: （用于 precious little、precious few）少得可怜
senses.definition: used before little or few to stress that there is far less of something than is wanted
senses.definitionCN: 用在 little 或 few 前，强调某物的数量比所需少得多
senses.example: There is precious little time left before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 离截止只剩少得可怜的一点时间。
senses.why: This ironic use grows out of the same scale: a precious thing should be plentiful, so calling a tiny amount precious underlines how little of it there is.
senses.whyCN: 这种反讽用法长在同一杆价值尺度上：珍贵的东西本该充足，偏说那一点点很「珍贵」，反而把「少」强调出来。

intro.en: Precious and price are twins from one Latin noun, pretium. English sent price down the market road and precious down the road of worth, which is why the two now feel unrelated.
intro.cn: precious 与 price 是同一个拉丁名词 pretium 生下的一对双胞胎。英语让 price 走上买卖的路，让 precious 走上价值的另一条路，所以今天两者听起来毫不相干。

items.en: Pretium meant the price or value assigned to a thing, and it could name both the money paid and the worth people believed a thing had.
items.cn: pretium 指给一件东西定下的价钱或价值，既能指付出的钱，也能指人们认为它值多少。

items.en: Pretiosus was built on pretium and described something of great worth, especially costly stones, metals and cloth.
items.cn: pretiosus 由 pretium 构成，形容价值很高的东西，尤指昂贵的宝石、金属与织物。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as precios, meaning costly and highly valued, and passed it to English in the medieval period.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 precios，意为昂贵的、极受重视的，并在中世纪传入英语。

items.en: Middle English precious kept the sense of great worth and began to be used for things valued for love rather than for money.
items.cn: 中古英语的 precious 保留「价值极高」的意思，并开始用于因感情而非金钱而宝贵的东西。

items.en: Modern English holds the split: price names what a thing costs, precious names what it is worth to someone, and the ironic precious little adds a third shade.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个分叉固定下来：price 指一件东西要多少钱，precious 指它对某人值多少，反讽的 precious little 又添了第三层色彩。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family that grew from Latin pretium; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for things people value.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语 pretium 长出来的同族词；近义组收人们用来形容「看重之物」的形容词。

entries.definition: The money a seller asks for something; it comes from the same Latin noun but took the commercial path.
entries.definitionCN: 卖方为一物索要的钱；与本词同出一个拉丁名词，但走的是买卖那条路。

entries.definition: To recognise the value of something, or to rise in value.
entries.definitionCN: 认识到某物的价值；也指升值。

entries.definition: A judgement of how much something is worth.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物价值的评估。

entries.definition: The quality of being precious, or of being over-refined.
entries.definitionCN: 珍贵的性质；也指做作讲究。

entries.definition: Worth a lot of money or of great use.
entries.definitionCN: 值很多钱的；很有用的。

entries.definition: Expensive, or causing loss and damage.
entries.definitionCN: 昂贵的；也指造成损失和破坏的。

entries.definition: Loved and kept with care over a long time.
entries.definitionCN: 长期被珍爱、被小心保存的。

entries.definition: Much loved, and in British English also expensive.
entries.definitionCN: 深受喜爱的；英式英语里也指昂贵的。

normalIntro.en: One Latin noun of value splits into a market word and a word of worth; the English adjective then climbs from treasure to taste, and finally to irony.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示价值的拉丁名词分成了市场词与价值词；英语形容词再从珍宝爬到品味，最后落到反讽。

normal.en: Pretium gives both price and precious, so the twins are cousins: one counts coins, the other counts what the coins cannot buy.
normal.cn: pretium 同时生出 price 与 precious，这对双胞胎是表亲：一个数钱，一个数钱买不到的东西。

normal.en: Precious metal and precious stone are fixed phrases: the material itself is the value.
normal.cn: precious metal 与 precious stone 是固定搭配，材料本身就是价值。

normal.en: Precious little means very little, and the word is doing the opposite of its usual job there.
normal.cn: precious little 意为「少得可怜」，在这里这个词做的正好是它平常相反的事。

normal.en: Preciousness adds -ness to name the quality, and it can be praise or a complaint about fussiness.
normal.cn: preciousness 加 -ness 表示性质，既可以是称赞，也可以是在抱怨过于讲究。

normal.en: Semiprecious keeps semi-, half, for stones such as amethyst that are valued but not in the first rank.
normal.cn: semiprecious 保留 semi-（半）这个成分，用于紫水晶这类有价值但不算头等的宝石。

abstract.en: Value has two doors: what a thing costs and what a thing means, and English gave each door its own word.
abstract.cn: 价值有两扇门：一件东西值多少钱，以及它意味着什么；英语给每扇门配了一个词。

abstract.en: When the word is used as an insult, it is because caring too much about small refinements looks like a false scale of value.
abstract.cn: 这个词用来损人时，是因为过分在意细枝末节，看起来像一杆失准的价值秤。

abstract.en: Precious little is a small joke built into the language: the more precious the thing, the sharper the complaint that there is almost none.
abstract.cn: precious little 是语言里自带的一个小玩笑：东西越珍贵，抱怨「几乎没有」就越扎人。

examples.en: Her grandmother's letters are the most precious thing she owns.
examples.cn: 祖母的信是她最珍视的东西。

examples.en: The box was inlaid with precious stones.
examples.cn: 这只盒子镶着宝石。

examples.en: There is precious little evidence for that claim.
examples.cn: 那个说法几乎没有证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普雷舍斯」——贵重东西捧在手里，舍不得放下；precious 就是珍贵的。

root: 拉丁语 pretium（价钱、价值）→ 形容词 pretiosus（价值高的）→ 古法语 precios → 英语 precious。同族的 price 走的是「买卖价钱」那一路，precious 走的是「本身可贵」这一路，两者同源而语义分叉。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow one scale of value: a treasured thing, an expensive material, a fussy attitude that overvalues small things, and an ironic phrase that turns value into scarcity.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项沿着同一杆价值尺度展开：被珍爱之物、昂贵材料、把小节看得过重的做作，以及把「珍贵」翻成「稀缺」的反讽说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn thimble resting in an open palm, its metal polished by years of use.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚磨旧的顶针躺在摊开的手掌上，金属被多年使用磨得发亮。

branches.en: a ring kept in a handkerchief and never worn
branches.cn: 手帕里那枚从不戴的戒指

branches.en: stones prised out of a crown to be weighed
branches.cn: 从王冠上撬下、拿去称重的宝石

branches.en: one value measured by love and one by money
branches.cn: 一份价值用感情量，一份用钱量

branches.en: a cup lifted by the handle with two fingers
branches.cn: 用两根手指捏着杯柄端起的杯子

branches.en: a clock with almost no time left on it
branches.cn: 只剩一点点时间的钟

intro.en: A Latin noun of value, an adjective suffix that says full of it, and a French reshaping carry the word into English; -ly and -ness then build the adverb and the noun.
intro.cn: 一个表示价值的拉丁名词、一个表示「充满」的形容词后缀，以及法语的一次改写，把这个词带进英语；-ly 与 -ness 再分别造出副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Pretium and its adjective pretiosus are well recorded, and the verb appretiare valued a thing; English inherited the family through French.
latinIntro.cn: pretium 及其形容词 pretiosus 都有清楚的记录，动词 appretiare 意为「估价」；英语经法语继承了这一族词。

items.meaning: in a precious or affected way

definition_zh: 精确的；准确的；明确的；严谨的；恰好的
definition_en: exact and accurate in detail; clearly defined and not approximate; careful about details
core_image: 一刀切下去，边缘干净，不多不少
scene: 这台仪器能把温度测到十分之一个刻度。The instrument can measure temperature to a precise tenth of a degree.
sceneCN: 这里 precise 是「精确到很小单位」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这台仪器能把温度测量到十分之一度的精确度。场景要点：刻度细、读数明确、没有模糊区间；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 精确的；准确的；明确的；严谨的

derivatives.zh: 精确；精密；精度
精确地；恰恰；正是
精确；严谨
不精确的；含糊的

senses.title: Exact in measurement
senses.titleCN: 精确的：读数细到很小一格
senses.definition: exact and accurate, with details measured or stated to a fine degree
senses.definitionCN: 精确而准确，细节被测量或陈述到很细的程度
senses.example: The instrument can measure temperature to a precise tenth of a degree.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器能把温度测量到十分之一度的精确度。
senses.why: Latin praecidere means to cut off. A precise measurement is one cut cleanly, with no ragged margin of doubt.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praecidere 意为“切掉”。精确的测量就是切得干净，边缘没有参差的疑问。

senses.title: Clearly defined and distinct
senses.definition: clearly stated or defined, so that there is no ambiguity
senses.definitionCN: 陈述或界定清楚，因而没有歧义
senses.example: The contract gives a precise definition of the delivery date.
senses.exampleCN: 合同对交付日期给出了明确的定义。
senses.why: If the edges are cut cleanly, the shape is unambiguous. A precise definition has no fuzzy border where other things could slip in.
senses.whyCN: 边缘切得干净，形状就不含糊。明确的定义没有模糊的边界，别的东西无从混入。

senses.title: Careful about small details
senses.titleCN: 严谨的：在小处也不放过
senses.definition: careful and exact in doing or describing something, paying attention to small details
senses.definitionCN: 在做或描述某事时仔细准确，注意细小之处
senses.example: She is precise about the order of the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 她对步骤的先后十分严谨。
senses.why: The cut-clean image becomes a habit of mind: refusing to let any detail stay rough.
senses.whyCN: “切得干净”的画面变成一种思维习惯：不允许任何细节保持粗糙。

senses.title: Strict about rules or standards
senses.titleCN: 讲究的：按规矩来，不将就
senses.definition: strict and particular about how things are done, often in matters of form
senses.definitionCN: 对做事方式严格挑剔，常指形式与礼数方面
senses.example: He was precise in his dress and punctual to the minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他衣着讲究，并且准时到分钟。
senses.why: A person who cuts every edge cleanly can become a person who insists on exact form. The trait shifts from result to temperament.
senses.whyCN: 一个把每条边都切干净的人，可能变成坚持确切形式的人。这个特征从结果转到了性情。

senses.title: Emphatic: the very same
senses.definition: used to emphasize that a particular thing or moment is exactly the one meant
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调所说的正是那一个事物或那一刻
senses.example: At that precise moment, the lights went out.
senses.exampleCN: 正是在那一刻，灯灭了。
senses.why: An exact point has no width. Using precise here says the moment cannot be widened into a general period.
senses.whyCN: 一个精确的点没有宽度。这里用 precise，是说那一刻无法被放宽成一段笼统的时期。

senses.title: Technical: high precision
senses.titleCN: 精密的：仪器能做到极细刻度
senses.definition: of an instrument or method, able to produce very exact results
senses.definitionCN: 指仪器或方法能给出非常精确的结果
senses.example: Precise instruments are required for this experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验需要精密的仪器。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to the tool that makes the clean cut. Precision becomes a property of the instrument, not only of the number.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词贴到了做出干净切割的工具上。精确性成了仪器的属性，而不只是数字的属性。

senses.title: Discourse: to be exact
senses.definition: in the phrase to be precise, used to correct or narrow what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 在 to be precise 这一短语中，用来修正或收窄刚才说过的话
senses.example: He arrived late, at ten past eight, to be precise.
senses.exampleCN: 他到得晚了，确切地说是八点十分。
senses.why: The speaker performs the cutting in speech: trimming a rough statement down to its exact edge.
senses.whyCN: 说话人在言语里执行这一刀：把粗略的说法修到确切的边缘。

senses.title: Neatly executed in movement or art
senses.titleCN: 动作精准：每一笔每一动都不含糊
senses.definition: performed with exact control, as in dance, surgery, or drawing
senses.definitionCN: 以精确的控制完成，如舞蹈、手术或绘画中的动作
senses.example: The dancer's precise movements made the whole phrase look effortless.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者精准的动作让整个乐句显得毫不费力。
senses.why: The body can cut cleanly too. Precision in movement is the same refusal of slack, expressed in muscle.
senses.whyCN: 身体也能切得干净。动作的精准是同一种对松弛的拒绝，只是用肌肉表达出来。

intro.en: Precise comes from a Latin participle meaning cut off. The path from 'cut short' to 'exact' is the story of a metaphor that became a standard.
intro.cn: precise 来自一个意为“被切掉”的拉丁分词。从“切短”到“精确”的路径，是一个比喻变成标准的历程。

items.en: Prae meant 'before, in front'. Here it intensifies rather than marks time: the cutting is done right at the front edge.
items.cn: prae 意为“在前”。这里它起加强作用而非标时间：这一刀正切在前沿上。

items.en: Caedere meant 'to cut, to strike'. English gets scissors, decide, concise, and circumcise from this family.
items.cn: caedere 意为“切、砍”。英语的 scissors、decide、concise、circumcise 都出自这个词族。

items.en: Praecidere meant 'to cut off, to cut short'. It described trimming something down to a clean limit.
items.cn: praecidere 意为“切掉、切短”。它描述把某物修到干净的界限。

items.en: The past participle praecisus meant 'cut off, shortened'. It is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.cn: 过去分词 praecisus 意为“被切掉的、被缩短的”。它是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.en: French used précis for 'cut short, concise, exact'. English borrowed the form in the 16th century.
items.cn: 法语用 précis 表示“切短的、简洁的、确切的”。英语在 16 世纪借入这个词形。

items.en: The sense moves from 'cut short' to 'definite' and then to 'accurate to a fine degree'. Modern usage applies it to numbers, definitions, instruments, people, and moments.
items.cn: 词义从“切短”转到“确定”，再转到“精确到很细的程度”。现代用法把它用于数字、定义、仪器、人以及时刻。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for cutting. The second group collects words for accuracy and exactness.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“切”的动词。第二组收表示准确与确切的词。

entries.definition: the quality of being exact, or the degree of exactness. It is the noun built on precise.
entries.definitionCN: 精确的性质，或精确的程度。它是建立在 precise 之上的名词。

entries.definition: exactly, or used to confirm a statement. Precisely can answer a question with a firm yes.
entries.definitionCN: 精确地，或用于确认某陈述。precisely 可以以干脆的“正是”来回答提问。

entries.definition: brief and clear. Con- 'together' plus caedere 'cut': cut down to essentials.
entries.definitionCN: 简短而清楚。con-“一起”加 caedere“切”：切到只剩要点。

entries.definition: to settle a question. De- 'off' plus caedere 'cut': cut off alternatives until one remains.
entries.definitionCN: 把问题定下来。de-“去掉”加 caedere“切”：切掉其他选项，直到只剩一个。

entries.definition: correct in every detail. Exact stresses correctness; precise stresses fine definition and care.
entries.definitionCN: 每个细节都正确。exact 强调正确；precise 强调界定细密与讲究。

entries.definition: correct and free from error. Accurate is about truth to fact; precise is about narrowness of specification.
entries.definitionCN: 正确且无错误。accurate 关乎与事实相符；precise 关乎规格的窄细。

entries.definition: clearly identified rather than general. Specific names the thing; precise describes how finely it is defined.
entries.definitionCN: 明确指出的，而非笼统的。specific 指名的是哪一个；precise 描述界定得多细。

entries.definition: showing great attention to detail. Meticulous fits sense 03 and stresses care rather than measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 对细节极为注意。meticulous 对应第 3 义项，强调用心而非测量。

entries.definition: clear and not uncertain. Definite fits sense 02 and is close to the 'cut clean' image.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而不含糊。definite 对应第 2 义项，贴近“切得干净”的画面。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the clean cut, the narrow definition, the meticulous person, the exact instant, and the phrase to be precise.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：干净的一刀、窄而清楚的定义、一丝不苟的人、正好的那一刻、以及 to be precise 这句话。

normal.en: Precise comes from a verb meaning to cut off. Picture a knife trimming away every loose edge.
normal.cn: precise 来自意为“切掉”的动词。想象一把刀把每一条松散的边都修掉。

normal.en: A precise definition has a clean border: nothing else can slip in.
normal.cn: 明确的定义有一条干净的边界：别的东西混不进来。

normal.en: Precise instruments are the ones whose readings do not wobble.
normal.cn: 精密的仪器，就是读数不会晃的那种。

normal.en: At that precise moment means the moment has no width; you cannot widen it into an afternoon.
normal.cn: at that precise moment 意为那一刻没有宽度，你不能把它放宽成一个下午。

normal.en: To be precise is to take the rough sentence and trim it to its exact edge.
normal.cn: to be precise 就是把粗糙的句子修到确切的边缘。

abstract.en: Precision is a relation between a statement and a tolerance, not a property of the world by itself.
abstract.cn: 精确是陈述与容许误差之间的关系，不是世界本身的属性。

abstract.en: Every precise definition is also an exclusion: to say exactly what it is, is to say what it is not.
abstract.cn: 每个明确的定义同时也是一次排除：说清它是什么，就是说清它不是什么。

abstract.en: The same cut that makes a thing exact can make it narrow; precision always trades scope for edge.
abstract.cn: 使事物精确的那一刀，也可能使它变窄；精确总是用范围换取边缘。

examples.en: The instructions were precise enough that a beginner could follow them.
examples.cn: 这些指示足够精确，初学者也能照着做。

examples.en: To be precise, the meeting lasted forty-two minutes.
examples.cn: 确切地说，会议持续了四十二分钟。

examples.en: Her precise handwriting filled the margins without a single correction.
examples.cn: 她精准的字迹填满了页边，没有一处涂改。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞赛斯”——普瑞在赛前把秒表按到千分之一秒，就是 precise（精确的）

root: 拉丁语 praecidere“切掉、切短”（prae“在前”+ caedere“切”）的过去分词 praecisus → 法语 précis → 英语 precise（16 世纪）；与 concise、decide、scissors 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a clean cut. A clean cut gives exact numbers, unambiguous definitions, meticulous habits, and instruments that do not wobble. The emphatic use fixes one instant, and to be precise performs the same trimming in speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是干净的一刀。干净的一刀给出精确的数字、不含糊的定义、一丝不苟的习惯，以及不晃的仪器。强调用法固定住某一刻，而 to be precise 是在言语里执行同一番修边。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade trimming an edge until nothing rough is left.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀刃修边，直到不剩一点毛糙。

branches.en: MEASURE: exact readings and the instruments that produce them.
branches.cn: 测量：精确的读数，以及产生这些读数的仪器。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: a definition with a clean edge, and a moment with no width.
branches.cn: 边界：边缘干净的定义，以及没有宽度的时刻。

branches.en: TEMPERAMENT: the meticulous person and the person strict about form.
branches.cn: 性情：一丝不苟的人，以及讲究形式的人。

branches.en: SPEECH: trimming a rough statement down to the exact word.
branches.cn: 言语：把粗略的说法修到确切的字眼。

branches.en: MOVEMENT: the same clean edge performed by the body.
branches.cn: 动作：由身体执行的同一种干净边缘。

intro.en: Precise is one participle from the cut family. The same verb, with different prefixes, gives concise, decide, and scissors.
intro.cn: precise 是“切”词族里的一个分词。同一个动词配上不同前缀，给出 concise、decide、scissors。

latinIntro.en: Latin praecisus reached English through French précis, which is why the English form lacks the Latin -us ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 praecisus 经法语 précis 到达英语，所以英语形式没有拉丁的 -us 词尾。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
表示状态或性质的名词后缀

definition_zh: 精确地；准确地；恰恰；正好；（回答时）正是如此；严谨地
definition_en: in an exact way with no approximation; exactly at a stated point; as a firm reply of agreement; and with careful attention to every detail
core_image: 秒针压住刻度线，分毫不差，指针停在那里没有再动
scene: 站台上的人都低头看表，广播响起时，秒针正好压在整点刻度上。The train pulled out at precisely nine o'clock, and the platform emptied within a minute.
sceneCN: 这里 precisely 指「恰好、正好在某一刻」（第 2 个义项：强调时间点分毫不差）；句意为列车恰好在九点整驶出，站台一分钟内就空了。图中可辨识场景：低头看表的人群、压在整点刻度上的秒针、迅速空下去的站台。

pos.zh: 精确地；准确地；恰恰；严谨地

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁分词 praecisus 经法语进入英语，义为「精确的；明确的」
由 precise 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「精确；精密度」
由 precise 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「精确；严谨」

senses.title: In an exact and accurate way
senses.definition: in a way that is exact in every detail and contains no approximation
senses.definitionCN: 每一个细节都准确，不含任何近似成分
senses.example: The instrument measures the temperature precisely.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器能精确测量温度。
senses.why: Latin praecidere meant to cut off, and its participle praecisus described something trimmed until nothing extra was left; an exact figure is exactly that, with every vague edge shaved away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praecidere 意为「切掉」，分词 praecisus 形容被削到不剩多余部分的东西；一个精确的数字正是如此，所有模糊的边角都被削掉了。

senses.title: Exactly, at one stated point
senses.definition: used to stress that something happens at exactly a stated time, place or manner and not merely near it
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调某事恰好在所说的时间、地点或方式上发生，而不是接近而已
senses.example: The power failed precisely at the moment the speech began.
senses.exampleCN: 就在演讲开始的那一刻，电停了。
senses.why: Once the word means with nothing left over, it can point to a single instant or a single spot, and the stress falls on the perfect fit between the words and the fact.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「不留余量」，它就能指向某一个瞬间或某一个点，重音落在「话与事实严丝合缝」上。

senses.title: Exactly so, as a reply of agreement
senses.definition: used alone as a firm reply to say that the other person has understood something completely
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用，作为肯定的回答，表示对方完全理解正确
senses.example: So the delay was caused by the missing signature? Precisely.
senses.exampleCN: 所以延误是因为少了那个签名？正是如此。
senses.why: The emphatic use shrinks into a one-word answer: agreeing that a description fits perfectly is the same act as measuring a perfect fit.
senses.whyCN: 强调用法再缩成一个单词的回答：承认对方的描述完全吻合，与「量出一个严丝合缝」本是同一个动作。

senses.title: With careful attention to every detail
senses.definition: in a way that shows careful attention to small details and a strict, orderly method
senses.definitionCN: 表现出对细小环节的留意，以及严格而有条理的做法
senses.example: She recorded every reading precisely, down to the last decimal.
senses.exampleCN: 她把每个读数都记到小数点最后一位。
senses.why: Cutting away excess also describes a person's working method: whoever trims every loose detail out of an account is working precisely.
senses.whyCN: 「削去多余」也能形容一个人的做法：谁把记录里每处含糊都削干净，谁就是在严谨地做事。

intro.en: Precisely is precise plus -ly, and precise goes back to a Latin verb of cutting: what is exact has had everything loose cut away.
intro.cn: precisely 是 precise 加 -ly；而 precise 可追溯到拉丁语里表示「切」的动词：所谓精确，就是把所有松散的余量都切掉。

items.en: Caedere meant to cut or to strike down, and it supplied a large number of Latin verbs about cutting, killing and deciding.
items.cn: caedere 意为切、砍倒，为拉丁语提供了大量与切割、杀戮、决断有关的动词。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, whether the position was in space or in rank.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前」，既可指空间靠前，也可指地位优先。

items.en: Praecidere joined the two: to cut off the front part, and so to shorten, to cut short, or to cut away what is extra.
items.cn: praecidere 把两者合起来：切掉前面一段，因此也表示截短、缩短、削去多余部分。

items.en: The participle praecisus meant cut off or cut short, and in learned use it came to describe a statement trimmed of everything vague.
items.cn: 分词 praecisus 意为被切掉的、被截短的，在学术用法里逐渐用来形容一段被削去所有含糊处的表述。

items.en: English borrowed precise in the sixteenth century and later added -ly; the adverb kept both the measuring sense and the emphatic one.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 precise，后来又加上 -ly；这个副词同时保留了「测量」义与「强调」义。

note.en: The look-alike group sets the adjective and its noun beside the negated form; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of accuracy and exactness.
note.cn: 形近组把本词所由来的形容词及其名词与否定式放在一起；近义组收表示准确与分毫不差的副词。

entries.definition: Exact in every detail; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 每个细节都准确；本副词所由来的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being exact, especially in measurement or work.
entries.definitionCN: 精确的性质，尤指测量或做工上的。

entries.definition: Not exact, or not clearly stated.
entries.definitionCN: 不精确的；表述不清的。

entries.definition: The state of being exact in wording or method.
entries.definitionCN: 措辞或方法上的精确。

entries.definition: In a way that is completely correct and leaves nothing out.
entries.definitionCN: 完全正确、毫无遗漏地。

entries.definition: In a way that is correct and free from error.
entries.definitionCN: 正确而无误差地。

entries.definition: Directly and with no doubt, as in squarely in the middle.
entries.definitionCN: 正正地、毫不含糊地，如正中间。

entries.definition: With strict care and a systematic method.
entries.definitionCN: 以严格而系统的方法。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a knife inside it: to be exact is to have cut away everything that does not belong to the fact.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词里藏着一把刀：所谓准确，就是把不属于事实的部分统统切掉。

normal.en: Caedere is to cut, and praecisus is cut short, so precise work is work with the loose ends removed.
normal.cn: caedere 是切，praecisus 是被截短，所以精确的活儿就是把毛边削掉的活儿。

normal.en: Precision adds -ion and names the quality; a watchmaker talks about precision, not about precisement.
normal.cn: precision 加 -ion 表示性质；表匠说的是 precision，而不是另造一个名词。

normal.en: Precisely at six and precisely because both stress a perfect fit, one of time and one of reason.
normal.cn: precisely at six 与 precisely because 都在强调严丝合缝，一个扣时间，一个扣理由。

normal.en: A one-word Precisely in conversation is the same judgement made aloud and then stopped.
normal.cn: 对话里单独一个 Precisely，就是把同一个判断说出声，然后就此打住。

normal.en: Imprecise is the word with in-, not exact and often slightly vague by accident.
normal.cn: imprecise 是加上 in- 的否定式，意为不精确，常带一点无意间含糊的意味。

abstract.en: Accuracy is subtraction, not addition: the word says so every time it is used.
abstract.cn: 准确是减法而不是加法：这个词每次被使用都在这样说。

abstract.en: A clock and an argument can both be precise, because both can be judged by how well the edges meet.
abstract.cn: 钟表和论证都可以很 precise，因为两者都能用「边角是否对齐」来判断。

abstract.en: When someone answers precisely, they are confirming that no word needs to be moved.
abstract.cn: 有人回答 precisely 时，是在确认这句话里没有一个词需要挪动。

examples.en: The instrument measures the temperature precisely.
examples.cn: 这台仪器能精确测量温度。

examples.en: The power failed precisely at the moment the speech began.
examples.cn: 就在演讲开始的那一刻，电停了。

examples.en: She recorded every reading precisely, down to the last decimal.
examples.cn: 她把每个读数都记到小数点最后一位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞赛斯利」——切得干净利落，一点毛边都不留；precisely 就是精确地。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ caedere（切）→ praecidere（切掉、截短）→ 分词 praecisus → 英语 precise → 加 -ly 成 precisely。同族有 precision、imprecise。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow one idea: everything extra has been cut away, so a figure is exact, a moment is exactly that moment, an answer is exactly right, and a method leaves no detail loose.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项沿着同一个念头展开：多余的部分都被切掉了，所以数字准确、时刻分毫不差、回答完全正确、做法不放过任何细节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second hand pressed against a mark on the dial, held there without the smallest drift.
core.cn: 核心意象：秒针压在表盘的刻度线上，停在那里，没有一丝偏移。

branches.en: a gauge needle settling on a hairline mark
branches.cn: 表针停在细如发丝的刻度上

branches.en: a switch thrown at the exact second a speech starts
branches.cn: 在演讲开始那一秒被拉下的开关

branches.en: a single word of agreement that ends the discussion
branches.cn: 一个词结束整场讨论

branches.en: a record book filled to the last decimal place
branches.cn: 记到小数点最后一位的记录本

branches.en: a measurement and a method both trimmed clean
branches.cn: 一次测量与一套做法都被修得干净

intro.en: A Latin verb of cutting, a prefix of being in front, and English -ly hold the word together; its family also gives the noun precision and the negated imprecise.
intro.cn: 一个表示切的拉丁动词、一个表示「在前」的前缀，加上英语的 -ly，共同撑起这个词；同族还有名词 precision 与否定式 imprecise。

latinIntro.en: Caedere, praecidere and the participle praecisus are all securely recorded Latin forms, so the family is well documented rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: caedere、praecidere 以及分词 praecisus 都是有可靠记录的拉丁语形式，所以这一族词有据可查，而非重构。

items.meaning: to cut off, to cut short

latinEntries.meaning: to cut off, to cut short

definition_zh: 精确；精密度；精确性；（仪器、测量的）精度；有效数字位数；（加工）公差
definition_en: the quality of being exact, especially the fineness of a measurement or the closeness of repeated readings to one another
core_image: 一把薄刃把多余的部分削掉，只留下真正要的那一点
scene: 实验室的台面上摆着一支滴定管、一本记录册和一台电子天平，同一份样品被反复称了五回。The precision of the balance showed in five readings that differed by less than a milligram.
sceneCN: 这里 precision 指「统计意义上的重复一致性」（第 2 个义项：重复测量的一致程度）；句意：这台天平的精密度体现在五次读数相差不到一毫克。图中可辨识物件：滴定管、记录册、电子天平、样品瓶；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 精确；精密度；精度；精确性

derivatives.zh: 精确的；确切的
精确地；恰好
精确；一丝不苟
不精确；不准确
不精确的

senses.title: The fineness of a stated measurement
senses.titleCN: 测量值本身的精细程度
senses.definition: the degree to which a stated measurement is divided into fine enough steps for two nearby values to be told apart
senses.definitionCN: 一个测量值被细分到多细的程度，即能否把两个接近的值区分开
senses.example: The precision of the reading was limited by the smallest mark on the ruler.
senses.exampleCN: 这个读数的精度受限于尺子上最小的那道刻度。
senses.why: Praecisio is a cutting off, and a finely stated measurement is one cut into narrow slices.
senses.whyCN: praecisio 本义是切去，精细报出的测量值就是把量切成一薄片一薄片。

senses.title: Repeatability across repeated measurements
senses.definition: in statistics, the closeness of repeated measurements to one another, whether or not they sit near the true value
senses.definitionCN: 统计上多次测量彼此接近的程度，与它们是否靠近真值无关
senses.example: The five runs showed high precision even when the average was slightly off.
senses.exampleCN: 五次运行即使平均值略有偏差，重复精密度依然很高。
senses.why: Statistics separates the scatter among repeats, called precision, from the distance to the truth, called accuracy.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把重复测量的分散程度称为精密度，把与真值的距离称为准确度，两者分开。

senses.title: The smallest step an instrument can show
senses.definition: the smallest change in a quantity that an instrument can register, display or resolve
senses.definitionCN: 仪器能够记录、显示或分辨的最小变化量
senses.example: The instrument's precision reaches one part in a million.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器的精度达到百万分之一。
senses.why: An instrument whose scale is cut more finely can separate values that a coarse one merges.
senses.whyCN: 刻度切得更细的仪器，能把粗仪器混在一起的值分开。

senses.title: Exactness in wording
senses.definition: careful exactness in the choice of words, so that a statement admits only one reading
senses.definitionCN: 用词上的细致准确，使一句话只容许一种读法
senses.example: She described the procedure with the precision of a manual.
senses.exampleCN: 她像操作手册一样精确地描述了步骤。
senses.why: Latin praecisio also meant brevity of speech, where every surplus word has been cut away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praecisio 也指言辞简省，即把多余的词都切掉。

senses.title: Targeted action on a small site
senses.titleCN: 精准农业与精准医疗的定点干预
senses.definition: an approach that directs water, treatment or medicine only to the exact field, place or patient that needs it
senses.definitionCN: 只把水、处理或药物投到确切需要的田块、地点或病人身上的做法
senses.example: Precision irrigation delivers water to the driest rows alone.
senses.exampleCN: 精准灌溉只把水送到最干的那几垄。
senses.why: The modern compounds keep the old image of a cut made exactly where it is wanted.
senses.whyCN: 现代复合词保留了老意象：只在需要的地方下刀。

senses.title: The number of reliable digits
senses.definition: the count of digits in a reported value that carry real information about how finely it is known
senses.definitionCN: 一个报告值中携带真实精细信息的数字位数
senses.example: Report the mean to four digits of precision.
senses.exampleCN: 把平均值报到四位有效数字。
senses.why: Digits past the reliable cut are noise, so counting the trustworthy digits states the precision.
senses.whyCN: 可靠切点之后的位只是噪声，数出可信位数就是在说明精度。

senses.title: Machining to a very small tolerance
senses.titleCN: 机械加工的公差与精度
senses.definition: the closeness with which a machined part matches its specified size, measured in very small units
senses.definitionCN: 加工件与规定尺寸吻合的紧密程度，以极小的单位计量
senses.example: The shop grinds bearings to a precision of two microns.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把轴承磨到两微米的精度。
senses.why: In a machine shop the abstract fineness becomes metal cut away until the part fits.
senses.whyCN: 在机加工车间，抽象的精细变成被切掉的金属，直到零件合适。

senses.title: Strict exactness in legal or formal form
senses.titleCN: 法律或形式上的严格精确
senses.definition: the strict following of exact wording or procedure, where no looseness or paraphrase is permitted
senses.definitionCN: 严格遵循确切的措辞或程序，不允许任何松动或改写
senses.example: The clause was drafted with precision to close every loophole.
senses.exampleCN: 这一条款起草得十分精确，堵住了每个漏洞。
senses.why: A legal cut must fall on exactly the right word, which is the original image applied to text.
senses.whyCN: 法律之刀必须落在确切的字上，正是原意象用在文本上。

intro.en: Precision comes from Latin praecisio 'a cutting off', a noun of action from praecidere 'to cut short', built on prae- 'in front' plus caedere 'to cut'. French carried the word into English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: precision 出自拉丁 praecisio「切去」，是 praecidere「切短」的动作名词，由 prae-「在前」加 caedere「切」构成。英语十六世纪经法语引入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Caedere meant 'to cut, to strike down'; it also underlies incision, excise and decision, each of which turns on a cut.
items.cn: caedere 意为「切、砍倒」，也构成 incision、excise 与 decision，这几个词都围绕「切」展开。

items.en: Prae- 'in front' plus caedere made praecidere 'to cut off in front, to shorten'; a speech that was praecisus had its surplus trimmed away.
items.cn: prae-「在前」加 caedere 构成 praecidere「切去前面、截短」；被称作 praecisus 的言辞就是把多余部分削掉了。

items.en: Praecisio named the act of cutting off and also brevity of style, so the notion of fine trimming sits inside both senses.
items.cn: praecisio 既指切去的动作，也指文风的简省，因此「削到恰好」的观念同时存在于这两层。

items.en: Middle French precision brought the word into English, first for concise speech and only later for exact measurement.
items.cn: 中古法语 precision 把这个词带进英语，先用于简练的言辞，较晚才用于精确测量。

items.en: Nineteenth-century science and manufacturing applied the word to instrument scales and machined parts, which produced the modern technical senses.
items.cn: 十九世纪的科学与制造业把这个词用到仪器刻度和加工零件上，现代技术义项由此形成。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the direct source is Latin praecisio, attested in the classical language, so the word itself is not in doubt; only the exact year of its first English use is not recorded. The usual route is through French, while a direct Latin borrowing is also argued; no single route is imposed here.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：直接来源是有据可查的拉丁语 praecisio，词本身并不存疑；只是英语最早用例的具体年份没有记录。通常认为经法语传入，也有直接借自拉丁语的说法；此处不强行选定单一传入路径。

note.en: Group one is the same Latin family seen through its adjective, adverb and negative forms; group two holds the measuring partners that share the field but answer a different question.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁词族在形容词、副词与否定形式上的样子；第二组是同处测量领域的伙伴词，但它们回答的是另一个问题。

entries.definition: Giving exact details with nothing vague; it describes the thing or the person, while precision names the quality itself.
entries.definitionCN: 给出确切细节、毫不含糊；它形容事物或人，而 precision 是这种性质本身。

entries.definition: In an exact way, or used as an emphatic 'exactly'; it modifies an action rather than naming a measured degree.
entries.definitionCN: 以确切的方式，或用作加强语气的「正是」；它修饰动作，不指一个测得的程度。

entries.definition: Lack of exactness, formed with the negative prefix im-; it is the direct opposite of precision in every sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不精确，由否定前缀 im- 构成；在各义项上都是 precision 的反面。

entries.definition: A less common synonym for precision, stressing the manner of being exact rather than a measured degree of fineness.
entries.definitionCN: precision 的罕用同义词，强调一丝不苟的作风，而非测得的精细程度。

entries.definition: How near a measurement lies to the true value; a rifle can be accurate while its shots are widely spread.
entries.definitionCN: 测量值与真值的接近程度；一支枪可以很准确，但弹着点散布很广。

entries.definition: The state of being wholly correct, often said of a figure or a copy rather than of a spread of repeats.
entries.definitionCN: 完全正确的状态，常用于数字或副本，而不是重复测量的散布。

entries.definition: The smallest interval an instrument or an image can distinguish; it is the hardware side of precision.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器或图像能分辨的最小间隔；它是精密度在硬件上的表现。

entries.definition: The range of variation a specification allows; precision is the aim, tolerance is the slack accepted around it.
entries.definitionCN: 规格允许的变动范围；precision 是瞄准的目标，tolerance 是允许的松量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin cut, the fine scale and the fixed phrases that keep the word technical.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语的「切」、细密的刻度，以及把这个词固定在技术语境里的搭配。

normal.en: Prae- 'before' plus caedere 'to cut': trim off the surplus.
normal.cn: prae-「在前」加 caedere「切」：把多余的部分削掉。

normal.en: A fine scale cuts a quantity into narrow slices.
normal.cn: 细密的刻度把一个量切成一薄片一薄片。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: precision measurement, precision instrument, precision farming.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：精密测量、精密仪器、精准农业。

normal.en: Statistics keeps precision for repeats and accuracy for the true value.
normal.cn: 统计学用「精密度」说重复，用「准确度」说真值。

normal.en: In a machine shop precision is measured in microns.
normal.cn: 在机加工车间，精度以微米计。

abstract.en: Picture a blade shaving a hair's width off a metal block.
abstract.cn: 想象刀刃从金属块上削下一根头发那么薄的一层。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose marks sit closer together than a fingernail.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子，刻度线比指甲还窄。

abstract.en: Picture five arrows in one tight cluster, though none of them near the bullseye.
abstract.cn: 想象五支箭扎在同一小簇里，却都不靠近靶心。

examples.en: The survey reported its margin with more precision than the sample size deserved.
examples.cn: 这项调查报出的误差范围，比它的样本量所能支撑的更为精细。

examples.en: Precision alone does not make a scale trustworthy if it was zeroed wrongly.
examples.cn: 如果零点调错了，光有精密度并不能让一台秤可信。

examples.en: Precision medicine matches a drug to the genetic profile of one patient.
examples.cn: 精准医疗把药物匹配到某一位病人的基因特征上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pre（在前）+ cise（切）」——把多余的部分切掉，留下的就是精确

root: 拉丁 praecisio「切去」= praecidere（prae-「在前」+ caedere「切」）的动作名词。同族词有 precise、precisely、preciseness、imprecision。英语经法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one cut: a finely stated value, statistical repeatability, an instrument's smallest step, exact wording, targeted action, reliable digits, machining tolerance and strict legal form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守着同一刀：精细报出的测量值、统计上的重复一致性、仪器的最小刻度、确切的措辞、定点干预、可靠位数、加工公差，以及法律形式上的严格精确。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin blade cutting away everything that is not the exact point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把薄刃削掉一切不属于那一点的部分。

branches.en: FINE DIVISIONS: stating a value in narrow steps and counting the reliable digits are the same cut seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 细分：把值报成窄小的台阶与数出可靠位数，是同一刀的两面。

branches.en: REPEATS AGREE: statistical precision is the spread among repeats, not the distance from the truth.
branches.cn: 重复一致：统计上的精密度是重复测量之间的散布，而不是与真值的距离。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT'S EDGE: a finer scale lets a device separate what a coarse one merges.
branches.cn: 仪器的刃口：刻度更细的装置能把粗装置混在一起的值分开。

branches.en: CLEAN WORDING: exact speech and strict legal form both cut off every second reading.
branches.cn: 干净的措辞：确切的表达与严格的法律形式，都切掉了第二种读法。

branches.en: ACTION AT ONE SPOT: precision farming and precision machining both demand the cut land where the work requires.
branches.cn: 定点下手：精准农业与精密加工都要求这一刀落在工作真正需要的地方。

intro.en: Precision is a Latin noun of action built from a prefix, a verb root and a suffix, and the same pieces also build the everyday adjectives precise and imprecise.
intro.cn: precision 是由前缀、动词词根与后缀构成的拉丁动作名词，同样的构件也造出日常形容词 precise 与 imprecise。

latinIntro.en: Prae- 'in front' plus caedere 'to cut' yields praecidere, and -io turns it into the action noun praecisio; English then adds -ly and -ness and negates the whole word with im-.
latinIntro.cn: prae-「在前」加 caedere「切」得到 praecidere，-io 把它变成动作名词 praecisio；英语再加上 -ly 与 -ness，并用 im- 否定整个词。

items.example: The prefix puts the cutting ahead of the thing cut.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把切割放在被切之物的前面。

items.example: Incision and excise share this verb.
items.exampleCN: incision 与 excise 共用这个动词。

items.example: A long speech could be cut down to a short one.
items.exampleCN: 一段长话可以被截短成几句。

items.example: The Latin noun already carried the idea of trimming to the right size.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已经含有「削到恰好」的意思。

items.example: The word moved from speech to instruments.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从言辞转到了仪器上。

items.example: A precise answer leaves no room for a second reading.
items.exampleCN: 确切的回答不给第二种读法留空间。
这些零件严丝合缝地拼在一起。

items.example: Any imprecision in the clock ruins the timing.
items.exampleCN: 时钟的任何不精确都会毁掉计时。

items.example: An imprecise word can start a quarrel.
items.exampleCN: 一个不准确的词就能引起争吵。

items.example: Her preciseness made the instructions easy to follow.
items.exampleCN: 她的一丝不苟让说明容易照着做。

definition_zh: 预测；预言；预报；预料；预示
definition_en: to say or state in advance that something will happen, especially on the basis of evidence or reasoning
core_image: 站在今天，用话把明天的那件事先说出来
scene: 经济学家预测明年的增长会放缓。Economists predict slower growth next year.
sceneCN: 这里 predict 是「依据数据对将来作出判断」（第 2 个义项：预测）；句意：经济学家预测明年增长会放缓。场景要点：用现有信息、指向未来、可被检验；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 预测；预言；预报；预料
作出预测；预言

derivatives.zh: 预测；预言
可预测的；意料之中的
预测者；预测指标
不可预测的；变化莫测的

senses.title: To say what will happen
senses.titleCN: 预测：先说将来会发生什么
senses.definition: to state in advance that a particular event will happen
senses.definitionCN: 事先说明某个特定事件将会发生
senses.example: No one could predict which team would win.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人能预测哪支队伍会赢。
senses.why: Latin praedicere is prae 'before' plus dicere 'say'. The plain sense is saying something before it becomes true.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praedicere 是 prae“在前”加 dicere“说”。最朴素的意思，就是在事情成真之前先把它说出来。

senses.title: To forecast from evidence
senses.titleCN: 预测：拿现有信息推算未来
senses.definition: to estimate a future state on the basis of data, models, or reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 依据数据、模型或推理估计未来的状况
senses.example: Economists predict slower growth next year.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家预测明年增长会放缓。
senses.why: The saying is not a guess but a calculation. Evidence is fed in, and the statement about the future comes out.
senses.whyCN: 这话不是猜的，而是算的。把证据喂进去，关于未来的陈述就出来了。

senses.title: Scientific prediction
senses.titleCN: 科学预言：理论先说出可检验的结果
senses.definition: to derive a testable consequence from a scientific theory before it is observed
senses.definitionCN: 在观察之前，从科学理论推出一个可检验的结果
senses.example: The theory predicted a new particle, which was found years later.
senses.exampleCN: 该理论预言了一种新粒子，数年后被找到。
senses.why: A good theory must be able to say what will be seen. Prediction is the test that separates science from speculation.
senses.whyCN: 好的理论必须能说出将会看到什么。预测是把科学与空想分开的那场考试。

senses.title: To indicate in advance by signs
senses.titleCN: 预示：迹象先替将来开口
senses.definition: to be a sign that something will happen, without anyone saying it in words
senses.definitionCN: 成为某事将会发生的迹象，而非由人用话说出
senses.example: Dark clouds predicted a heavy storm.
senses.exampleCN: 乌云预示着大风暴。
senses.why: Signs can speak. When the world itself shows what is coming, we extend the verb from the speaker to the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 迹象也能说话。当世界本身显露出即将发生的事，我们就把这个动词从说话者扩展到证据上。

senses.title: To prophesy
senses.titleCN: 预言：以先知的口吻宣告
senses.definition: to foretell future events as a prophet or oracle does, often without evidence
senses.definitionCN: 像先知或神谕那样预告未来，常无证据支持
senses.example: The old woman predicted that the drought would last seven years.
senses.exampleCN: 老妇人预言旱情会持续七年。
senses.why: The same act of speaking first, but the authority comes from revelation rather than from data.
senses.whyCN: 同样是先说出口的动作，只是权威来自启示而非数据。

senses.title: To expect or anticipate
senses.titleCN: 预料：心里已经先把它算上
senses.definition: to expect something to happen, often in everyday planning
senses.definitionCN: 预期某事会发生，常用于日常安排
senses.example: We predicted heavy traffic and left an hour early.
senses.exampleCN: 我们预料会堵车，所以提前一小时出发。
senses.why: Prediction need not be public. Private anticipation is the same forward-looking move, kept inside the head.
senses.whyCN: 预测不必公开。私下的预料是同一个朝前的动作，只是留在脑子里。

senses.title: Statistics: to estimate a value
senses.definition: to produce an estimated value for a future or unknown observation from a model
senses.definitionCN: 用模型为未来或未知的观测给出一个估计值
senses.example: The model predicts sales of 12,000 units in the first quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 模型预测第一季度销量为一万二千件。
senses.why: In statistics the prediction is a number with an interval, not a sentence. The verb becomes a technical operation.
senses.whyCN: 在统计学里，预测是一个带区间的数，而不是一句话。这个动词变成了一项技术操作。

senses.title: To warn in advance
senses.titleCN: 预告：提前提醒，好让人准备
senses.definition: to announce something in advance so that people can prepare for it
senses.definitionCN: 事先告知某事，以便人们可以准备
senses.example: The report predicted shortages and urged hospitals to stock up.
senses.exampleCN: 报告预告了短缺，并敦促医院囤货。
senses.why: Saying it early has a use: it buys time. Prediction becomes a warning when the future it names is unwelcome.
senses.whyCN: 提前说出来是有用的：它买来时间。当所命名的未来不受欢迎时，预测就成了预警。

intro.en: Predict is a Latin compound meaning to say beforehand. It is one of a large family built on the verb dicere, to say.
intro.cn: predict 是一个意为“事先说出”的拉丁复合词。它属于一个建立在动词 dicere（说）之上的大词族。

items.en: Dicere meant 'to say, declare'. It is the source of diction, dictionary, verdict, contradict, and predict.
items.cn: dicere 意为“说、宣告”。它是 diction、dictionary、verdict、contradict、predict 的来源。

items.en: Prae meant 'before, in front'. Joined to a verb of saying, it produces the sense of saying something before its time.
items.cn: prae 意为“在前”。与表示“说”的动词结合，就产生“在时间之前说出来”的意思。

items.en: Praedicere meant 'to make known beforehand, to declare in advance'. It was used for foretelling as well as for public proclamation.
items.cn: praedicere 意为“事先让人知道、预先宣告”。它既用于预言，也用于公开宣布。

items.en: The past participle praedictus meant 'foretold'. English keeps it inside words like prediction and predictably.
items.cn: 过去分词 praedictus 意为“被预言的”。英语把它保留在 prediction、predictably 这类词里。

items.en: English predict appears in the 16th century, at first in religious and learned writing about foretelling. The modern data-based sense develops much later.
items.cn: 英语 predict 出现于 16 世纪，最早见于谈论预言的宗教与学术写作。以数据为基础的现代义要晚得多才发展出来。

items.en: With the rise of science and statistics, predict becomes the standard word for evidence-based foretelling, while prophesy remains the religious term.
items.cn: 随着科学与统计的兴起，predict 成了“有据预告”的标准词，而 prophesy 保持宗教色彩。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for saying. The second group collects words for foretelling, each with a different basis of authority.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“说”的动词。第二组收表示“预告”的词，各自依据的权威不同。

entries.definition: a statement about what will happen. It is the noun built on predict with -ion.
entries.definitionCN: 关于将会发生什么的陈述。它是 predict 加 -ion 构成的名词。

entries.definition: able to be foreseen, often with a hint of dullness. Predict plus -able.
entries.definitionCN: 可以被预见的，常带一点乏味的暗示。predict 加 -able。

entries.definition: the part of a sentence that says something about the subject, or to base something on. It comes from Latin praedicare, a cousin of praedicere.
entries.definitionCN: 句子中陈述主语的部分，或“以……为依据”。它来自拉丁 praedicare，是 praedicere 的近亲。

entries.definition: a decision or judgement. Ver- 'true' plus dict 'said': what is said as true.
entries.definitionCN: 裁决或判定。ver-“真”加 dict“说”：被说成真实的话。

entries.definition: to say what is likely in weather, economics, or other systems. Forecast is common for weather and trends; predict is the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 预告天气、经济或其他系统的可能状况。forecast 多用于天气与趋势；predict 是一般用语。

entries.definition: to tell of a future event. Foretell is literary and often implies a sign or a seer.
entries.definitionCN: 讲述未来的事件。foretell 带文学色彩，常暗示有征兆或预言者。

entries.definition: to foretell under divine inspiration. Prophesy claims a religious authority that predict does not.
entries.definitionCN: 在神圣启示下预告未来。prophesy 主张一种宗教权威，predict 没有这种主张。

entries.definition: to expect something and often act in advance. Anticipate adds preparation; predict can be purely a statement.
entries.definitionCN: 预期某事并常提前行动。anticipate 多出“准备”之意；predict 可以只是陈述。

entries.definition: to estimate future figures from present trends. Project is technical and numerical, closer to sense 07.
entries.definitionCN: 由当前趋势估算未来数字。project 是技术性、数值性的，更接近第 7 义项。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the sentence said too early, the economist's model, the particle found later, the dark clouds, and the shopping list made before the rush.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：提早说出的那句话、经济学家的模型、后来找到的粒子、乌云、以及抢购前先列好的清单。

normal.en: Pre- means before, dict means say. Predict is say-before.
normal.cn: pre- 是“在前”，dict 是“说”。predict 就是“先说”。

normal.en: A weather forecast and a stock forecast are both predict with numbers plugged in.
normal.cn: 天气预报和股市预测，都是把数字代进去的 predict。

normal.en: A theory predicts a particle, then the lab goes looking for it. Prediction is the theory's exam.
normal.cn: 理论预言一种粒子，实验室随后去找它。预测就是理论的那场考试。

normal.en: Dark clouds predict rain without saying a word: signs can also speak.
normal.cn: 乌云一言不发就预示下雨：迹象也会说话。

normal.en: Predicting a rush and leaving early is the same verb, just kept private.
normal.cn: 预料拥堵并提早出门，是同一个动词，只是留在心里。

abstract.en: Every prediction is a promise the present makes about the future, and it can be broken by a single unforeseen event.
abstract.cn: 每个预测都是现在对未来作出的承诺，而它可能被一个未预见的事件打破。

abstract.en: The difference between prophecy and prediction is not the content but the warrant: revelation versus evidence.
abstract.cn: 预言与预测的差别不在内容，而在凭据：是启示，还是证据。

abstract.en: To predict well is to be willing to be wrong in public, which is why science prizes it.
abstract.cn: 预测得好，意味着愿意在公众面前出错；正因如此，科学看重它。

examples.en: The model predicts that sea levels will rise by about half a metre this century.
examples.cn: 该模型预测本世纪海平面将上升约半米。

examples.en: As predicted, the first frost came in the last week of October.
examples.cn: 正如所料，初霜在十月最后一周到来。

examples.en: Analysts predict a sharp fall in demand for new cars.
examples.cn: 分析人士预测新车需求将大幅下降。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞迪克特”——普瑞提前把“迪克特”那件事说出口，就是 predict（预测）

root: 拉丁语 praedicere“事先说出、预先宣告”＝prae“在前”+ dicere“说” → 英语 predict（16 世纪）；与 diction、dictionary、verdict、contradict 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The word always means saying something before it happens. What changes is the basis: evidence, theory, signs, revelation, private expectation, or a statistical model. Each basis gives a slightly different shade of the same forward-speaking act.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词始终指“在事情发生之前先说出来”。变化的是依据：证据、理论、征兆、启示、私下预期，或统计模型。每一种依据都给同一个“朝前说话”的动作一种不同的色调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence spoken today about an event that has not yet arrived.
core.cn: 核心意象：今天说出一句话，说的是尚未到来的事件。

branches.en: SPEECH: saying or expecting, public or private.
branches.cn: 言语：说出或预料，公开或私下。

branches.en: CALCULATION: forecasts from data, and statistical estimates.
branches.cn: 计算：由数据作出的预报，以及统计估计。

branches.en: SCIENCE: the theory that names a result before it is observed.
branches.cn: 科学：在结果被观察之前就把它命名的理论。

branches.en: SIGN AND WARNING: the world speaking through evidence, and the early notice that buys time.
branches.cn: 征兆与预警：世界借证据说话，以及买来时间的提前告知。

branches.en: PROPHECY: the same act, warranted by revelation.
branches.cn: 预言：同一个动作，凭据是启示。

intro.en: Predict is one compound from the large dicere family. Every word below is either a piece of that compound or a sibling built with another prefix on the same verb of saying.
intro.cn: predict 是 dicere 大词族里的一个复合词。下面每个词，要么是这个复合词的构件，要么是在同一个“说”的动词上加别的前缀构成的兄弟词。

latinIntro.en: Latin praedicere and its participle praedictus supplied the English forms; the same dic- stem appears across law, grammar, and everyday speech.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 praedicere 及其分词 praedictus 提供了英语形式；同一个 dic- 词干出现在法律、语法与日常言语中。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀

definition_zh: 可预测的；可预料的；意料之中的；平淡老套的；规律稳定的
definition_en: able to be known or stated in advance; happening as everyone already expects; too regular to be interesting; and steady enough to be relied on
core_image: 老人的手在桌面上按同一节奏敲着，节拍一下都不差
scene: 老朋友聚会，话题总是从天气开始，再绕回谁又长胖了、谁换了工作。The conversation followed its predictable course: weather first, then who had gained weight.
sceneCN: 这里 predictable 指「可预料的、不出所料的」（第 2 个义项：事情按大家预想的样子发生）；句意为谈话照着可以预料的路子走：先说天气，再说谁胖了。图中可辨识场景：围坐的老朋友、从天气开头的话题、彼此打趣的笑声。

pos.zh: 可预测的；可预料的；平淡老套的；规律稳定的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 praedicere 经英语改造而来，义为「预言；预测」
由 predict 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「预言；预测」
由 predictable 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可预测性」
由否定前缀 un- 与 predictable 复合而成，义为「不可预测的」

senses.title: Able to be stated in advance
senses.titleCN: 可预测的；可以预先断定的
senses.definition: able to be known or worked out in advance because the evidence or the pattern allows it
senses.definitionCN: 因为证据或规律足够，所以能够提前知道或推算出来
senses.example: The tide is predictable to within a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水涨落的时间可以预测到几分钟之内。
senses.why: Latin praedicere meant to say something beforehand, and -able turns that act into a possibility: whatever can be said before it happens is predictable.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praedicere 意为「预先说出」，-able 把这个动作变成一种可能性：凡能在发生之前被说出来的，就是可预测的。

senses.title: Happening as everyone already expects
senses.titleCN: 意料之中的；不出所料的
senses.definition: happening in the way most people already expect, so that it causes no surprise when it does
senses.definitionCN: 按多数人早已预想的样子发生，真的发生时谁都不觉意外
senses.example: The ending of the film was predictable from the first scene.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的结局从第一场戏就能料到。
senses.why: If a thing can be said before it happens, then when it happens nobody is surprised; the sense slides from what can be foretold to what is simply unsurprising.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既然能在发生前被说出来，它真的发生时谁也不会吃惊；词义就从「可以预言」滑到「本来就没什么意外」。

senses.title: Too regular to be interesting
senses.definition: too regular or conventional to hold interest, showing no invention and no surprise
senses.definitionCN: 过于规律或循规蹈矩，因而提不起兴趣，既无新意也无意外
senses.example: Critics called the sequel predictable and safe.
senses.exampleCN: 评论界说这部续集平淡无趣、四平八稳。
senses.why: A pattern regular enough to be foretold soon becomes a pattern with nothing new inside it, and the same adjective turns into mild blame.
senses.whyCN: 一个规律到能被预言的格局，很快就变成内里没有新东西的格局，同一个形容词于是带上轻微的责备。

senses.title: Steady enough to be relied on
senses.definition: of a supply, income or person: behaving in a steady way that plans can be built on
senses.definitionCN: 指供给、收入或人行为稳定，可以照着它做计划
senses.example: Farmers here prefer a predictable supply of water to a lucky season.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农户更想要稳定的供水，而不是碰运气的丰水季。
senses.why: When the certainty is useful rather than boring, the word becomes praise: a predictable supply is one that a plan can be built on.
senses.whyCN: 当这种确定性是有用的而不是无聊的，这个词就变成称赞：可预测的供给，就是能照着它做计划的供给。

intro.en: Predictable is predict plus -able. The Latin verb behind predict meant to say a thing beforehand, and English first used it for declaring rather than for foretelling.
intro.cn: predictable 是 predict 加 -able。predict 背后的拉丁动词意为「预先说出」，而英语最初用它表示宣称、断言，并非预言。

items.en: Dicere meant to say or to declare, and it stands behind a very large family of English words about speech.
items.cn: dicere 意为说、宣称，是英语里一大批与言语有关的词的源头。

items.en: Praedicare joined prae-, before, with dicere: to say beforehand, and also to proclaim something publicly.
items.cn: praedicare 把 prae-（在前）与 dicere 结合：预先说出，也指当众宣告。

items.en: The noun praedictio meant a foretelling or a prophecy, and it kept the solemn tone of announcing what is to come.
items.cn: 名词 praedictio 意为预言、预告，保留了宣告未来之事的庄重语气。

items.en: English predict first meant to declare or assert something, and only later settled on foretelling the future.
items.cn: 英语 predict 最早意为宣称、断言某事，后来才固定为「预言未来」。

items.en: The adjective was formed with -able in the nineteenth century, first for events, then for people and their dull habits.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十九世纪由 -able 构成，先用于事件，随后用于人及其乏味的习惯。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb of saying through the English family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what can be counted on.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「说」的拉丁动词，收它在英语里的一族词；近义组收表示「可以指望」的形容词。

entries.definition: To say what will happen before it does.
entries.definitionCN: 在事情发生之前说出它会发生。

entries.definition: A statement about what will happen in the future.
entries.definitionCN: 关于将来会发生什么的说法；预言。

entries.definition: Impossible to know in advance, often changing without warning.
entries.definitionCN: 无法提前知道的；常指变化无常。

entries.definition: The quality of being able to be known in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 可以提前知道的性质；可预测性。

entries.definition: Able to be known or expected in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 能够提前知道或料到的。

entries.definition: Thought likely to happen or to be the case.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为很可能发生或属实的。

entries.definition: Following a fixed pattern, with equal gaps between events.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定规律出现的；间隔均匀的。

entries.definition: Ordinary, repeated and part of the usual order of things.
entries.definitionCN: 平常而反复的，属于常规安排的。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from a Latin verb of saying beforehand, so its centre is speech: what can be said in advance, and then what has nothing left to say.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「预先说出」的拉丁动词上，中心是「说」：能提前说出来的，以及后来没什么可说的。

normal.en: Dicere is to say and prae- is before, so predict is literally to say before, and -able makes it possible to do so.
normal.cn: dicere 是说，prae- 是在前，所以 predict 字面就是「预先说」，-able 让它成为「可以预先说的」。

normal.en: Prediction is the noun in -ion, and it can be a weather forecast or a prophecy.
normal.cn: prediction 是加 -ion 的名词，可以是天气预报，也可以是预言。

normal.en: Unpredictable adds un-, and it is the word used for weather, toddlers and market prices.
normal.cn: unpredictable 加了否定前缀 un-，天气、幼儿和市场价格都常被这样形容。

normal.en: Predictability names the quality, and planners pay for it in supply chains.
normal.cn: predictability 指这种性质，供应链上的规划者愿意为它花钱。

normal.en: Predictable income is praise, predictable plot is blame: the same word, two directions of judgement.
normal.cn: predictable income 是称赞，predictable plot 是贬斥：同一个词，两个方向的评价。

abstract.en: To predict is to speak before the event; to be predictable is to leave the future no room to speak.
abstract.cn: predict 是在事情之前说话；predictable 则是不给未来留下说话的空间。

abstract.en: The word measures the distance between what we know and what happens, and that distance can be comfort or boredom.
abstract.cn: 这个词量的是「我们所知」与「实际发生」之间的距离，而这段距离可以是安心，也可以是无聊。

abstract.en: A predictable world is easy to live in and hard to be surprised by, and the adjective holds both halves.
abstract.cn: 可预测的世界住起来省心，却很难再有惊喜，这个形容词把两半都装着。

examples.en: The tide is predictable to within a few minutes.
examples.cn: 潮水涨落的时间可以预测到几分钟之内。

examples.en: The ending of the film was predictable from the first scene.
examples.cn: 这部电影的结局从第一场戏就能料到。

examples.en: Farmers here prefer a predictable supply of water.
examples.cn: 这里的农户更喜欢稳定的供水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞迪克特波」——提前把话说明白，事情照着走；predictable 就是可预测的。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ dicere（说）→ praedicere（预先说出）→ 名词 praedictio（预言）→ 英语 predict → 加 -able 成 predictable。同族有 prediction、unpredictable。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move along one line: what can be said in advance, what therefore surprises nobody, what becomes dull through repetition, and what is steady enough to build a plan on.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项沿着一条线移动：能提前说出的，因此谁都不意外的，因重复而变得乏味的，以及稳定到可以据之做计划的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old hand tapping the table in the same rhythm, beat after beat, without one missed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只苍老的手在桌面上按同一节奏敲着，一下接一下，一次不差。

branches.en: a tide table marked to the minute
branches.cn: 精确到分钟的潮汐表

branches.en: an audience guessing the ending before it comes
branches.cn: 观众在结局到来前就猜到了

branches.en: a sequel that repeats every turn of the first film
branches.cn: 把第一部每个转折都重来一遍的续集

branches.en: an irrigation channel running on schedule
branches.cn: 按日程放水的灌溉渠

branches.en: a forecast and a supply both trusted enough to plan with
branches.cn: 一份预报与一份供给都可靠到能据之做计划

intro.en: A Latin verb of saying and a prefix meaning before make the verb; English -able then turns the act of foretelling into a quality, and -ity and un- extend the family.
intro.cn: 一个表示「说」的拉丁动词和一个表示「在前」的前缀造出动词；英语的 -able 再把「预言」这个动作变成性质，-ity 与 un- 又扩展了这一族。

latinIntro.en: Dicere, praedicere and praedictio are all recorded Latin forms, so the family is documented rather than reconstructed; only the English adjective is recent.
latinIntro.cn: dicere、praedicere 与 praedictio 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，所以这一族词有据可查，并非重构；只有英语形容词是较晚才有的。

definition_zh: 前言；序言；引言；为……作序；以……作为开场；前奏
definition_en: the introductory part of a book, the act of writing one, and an event or remark that comes before and introduces something larger
core_image: 书页刚翻开，第一行字略小，页边留白很宽
scene: 旧书摊上那本诗集的封面已经卷边，翻开第一页，作者的字迹还很清楚。In the preface the poet thanked the friend who had kept his early drafts.
sceneCN: 这里 preface 指「前言、序言」（第 1 个义项：正文之前由作者写的引子）；句意为诗人在序言里感谢那位替他保存早期草稿的朋友。图中可辨识物件：卷边的封面、第一页上略小的字、宽阔的页边留白。

pos.zh: 前言；序言；引言；前奏
为……作序；以……作为开场

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 praefari 加形容词后缀 -ory 构成，义为「引言性的；开场的」
由 preface 加表示人的 -er 构成，义为「写序言的人」
由 preface 加 -ed 构成的过去分词作定语，义为「带有序言的」

senses.title: The introductory part of a book
senses.definition: the short section at the beginning of a book, usually written by the author to explain its aim, method or history
senses.definitionCN: 书开头的一段短文，通常由作者说明写作目的、方法或成书经过
senses.example: In the preface she explains why the study took twelve years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在前言里说明了这项研究为何花了十二年。
senses.why: Latin praefatio was a saying beforehand, and a book's opening words are exactly that: the author speaks before the argument proper begins.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praefatio 就是「预先说的话」，一本书开头那几句正是如此：作者在正文论证真正开始之前先开口。

senses.title: To write a preface for a book
senses.definition: to write or provide a short introduction for a book, usually one written by someone else
senses.definitionCN: 为一本书撰写或提供短序，通常是替别人写的
senses.example: A retired professor prefaced the new edition.
senses.exampleCN: 一位退休教授为这个新版本作了序。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb without adding a single letter, because English lets the name of a thing become the act of putting that thing there.
senses.whyCN: 名词不添一个字母就变成动词，因为英语允许把一件事物的名字直接用成「把它放上去」的动作。

senses.title: Words or events that come first
senses.definition: something said or done before a larger event, serving to introduce it
senses.definitionCN: 在更大的事件之前说出或做出、起引子作用的话或事
senses.example: He prefaced his question with a long account of his own week.
senses.exampleCN: 他先讲了一大段自己这一周的经历，才把问题提出来。
senses.why: Anything that speaks before the main thing can be called a preface, so the word leaves the book and comes to name a conversational or historical opening.
senses.whyCN: 凡是抢在正事之前开口的东西都能叫 preface，于是这个词离开书本，转而指谈话或历史事件的开场。

intro.en: Preface goes back to a Latin verb of solemn speech: prae- before plus fari to speak, so the word has always meant words placed in front of other words.
intro.cn: preface 可追溯到拉丁语里表示郑重说话的动词：prae-（在前）加 fari（说），所以这个词一直指放在别的话前面的那段话。

items.en: Fari meant to speak or to utter, and it was an old religious and legal verb for saying something with weight.
items.cn: fari 意为说话、说出，是一个古老的宗教与法律用语，指有分量地讲出某事。

items.en: Prae- meant before, in place as well as in time, and it is the same prefix found in predict and prevent.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前」，空间和时间都可用，predict 与 prevent 里也是这个前缀。

items.en: Praefari meant to say something first, especially a formula spoken before a rite or a formal speech.
items.cn: praefari 意为先说出某话，尤指仪式或正式演讲之前先念的套语。

items.en: The noun praefatio named that preliminary saying, and later the written introduction placed before a work.
items.cn: 名词 praefatio 指这番预先的开场话，后来又指放在作品前面的书面引言。

items.en: English took the word through Old French preface, first for a spoken opening and soon for the opening pages of a book.
items.cn: 英语经古法语 preface 借入这个词，先指口头的开场，很快又指一本书开头的几页。

note.en: The look-alike group sets the word's own relatives beside two near-spellings from other Latin stems; the near-meaning group gathers names for the parts placed before a main text.
note.cn: 形近组把本词自己的同族词与两个来自其他拉丁词干的近形词放在一起；近义组收「放在正文之前那部分」的各种名称。

entries.definition: Serving as an introduction, especially at the start of a book.
entries.definitionCN: 起引言作用的，尤指书前的。

entries.definition: Having a preface, or introduced by one.
entries.definitionCN: 带有序言的；由序言开头的。

entries.definition: An official in charge of a district or a school; from Latin praefectus, a different stem, so the likeness is only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 负责一个地区或学校的官员；出自拉丁语 praefectus，词干不同，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A group of letters added to the front of a word; it shares prae- but not fari, so the likeness is only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 加在词首的一组字母；它与本词共用 prae-，但并非出自 fari，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A short introduction to a book, usually written by someone other than the author.
entries.definitionCN: 书前的短序，通常由作者以外的人撰写。

entries.definition: The opening part of a book that sets out its subject and purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 书的开头部分，用来说明主题与目的。

entries.definition: The opening section of a play or long poem, spoken before the main action.
entries.definitionCN: 戏剧或长诗开篇、在正戏之前说出的部分；开场白。

entries.definition: An introductory statement placed before a speech, a law or an agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 演讲、法律或协议之前的引言。

normalIntro.en: The word is two Latin pieces and nothing else: before plus speak. Every sense keeps that order, words set in front of other words.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是两块拉丁部件，没有别的：在前 加 说。每个义项都守着这个次序，把话放在别的话前面。

normal.en: Prae- is before and fari is to speak, so a preface is literally the speaking that comes first.
normal.cn: prae- 是在前，fari 是说，所以 preface 字面就是「最先说的那番话」。

normal.en: A preface is usually the author's own; a foreword is usually someone else's, which is why both exist.
normal.cn: preface 通常是作者自己写的，foreword 通常由别人写，两个词因此并存。

normal.en: Prefatory adds -ory and means of the nature of an introduction, as in a prefatory note.
normal.cn: prefatory 加 -ory，意为「引言性质的」，如 prefatory note（引言性说明）。

normal.en: Preface the book with a quotation turns the noun into a verb of arranging what comes first.
normal.cn: 把名词用作动词说「以一句引文为这本书作序」，讲的就是安排什么排在前面。

normal.en: Prefaced by applause describes a speech, and the picture is still an opening placed in front.
normal.cn: prefaced by applause 形容一场演讲，画面仍然是「放在前面的开场」。

abstract.en: A preface is a doorway built out of words: you pass through it before you enter the book.
abstract.cn: 序言是用话搭出来的一道门：进书之前先穿过它。

abstract.en: The word treats every beginning as a smaller thing standing in front of a larger one.
abstract.cn: 这个词把每个开端都看成一个小东西，立在一个更大的东西前面。

abstract.en: Because prae- is shared with predict, both words are about speaking ahead; only one speaks about the book and one about the future.
abstract.cn: 因为与 predict 共用 prae-，两个词都关于「提前说」；只是一个说书，一个说未来。

examples.en: In the preface she explains why the study took twelve years.
examples.cn: 她在前言里说明了这项研究为何花了十二年。

examples.en: A retired professor prefaced the new edition.
examples.cn: 一位退休教授为这个新版本作了序。

examples.en: He prefaced his question with a long account of his week.
examples.cn: 他先讲了一大段自己这一周的经历，才提出问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞法斯」——翻开书先「预先说法」；preface 就是前言，也能当动词表示作序。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ fari（说）→ praefari（先说）→ praefatio（开场话、引言）→ 古法语 preface → 英语 preface。同族有 prefatory。

sensesIntro.en: The senses keep one position: in front. Words in front of a book, the act of putting them there, and any remark or event that opens something larger.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项守着同一个位置：在前面。放在书前的话、把话放到书前的动作，以及为更大事件开场的话或事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a book opened at the first page, its type a little smaller, the margin left wide.
core.cn: 核心意象：书翻到第一页，字略小一些，页边留出很宽的空白。

branches.en: a first page whose type is smaller than the rest
branches.cn: 第一页字号比正文小的书

branches.en: a pen signing the name under a short opening note
branches.cn: 在简短开场白下签名的笔

branches.en: a long story told before the real question
branches.cn: 在真正的问题之前讲的一大段

branches.en: an opening note and an opening remark, both placed first
branches.cn: 一段书前的话与一段开场的话，都放在最前

branches.en: an editor asking a senior scholar for a few pages
branches.cn: 编辑请一位老学者写几页序

intro.en: Two Latin pieces, before and speak, make the noun; English then adds -ed and -er, while the older Latin adjective survives as prefatory.
intro.cn: 两块拉丁部件「在前」与「说」造出名词；英语再加 -ed 与 -er，而更早的拉丁形容词则以 prefatory 的形式留存。

latinIntro.en: Fari, praefari and praefatio are recorded Latin forms, and the adjective prefatory keeps the Latin suffix -ory; nothing here needs reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: fari、praefari 与 praefatio 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，形容词 prefatory 还保留着拉丁后缀 -ory；这里没有需要重构的部分。

definition_zh: 更喜欢；宁愿；优先考虑；提出（控告、索赔）；提拔（旧义）；按自己的判断决定
definition_en: to like one thing more than another, or to choose it rather than the alternative
