senses.title: Like one thing more than another
senses.definition: to like or want one thing more than another
senses.definitionCN: 比另一件东西更喜欢或更想要某一件
senses.example: She prefers tea to coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 比起咖啡，她更喜欢茶。
senses.why: Prae- means before and ferre means to carry, so the liked thing is carried in front of the other in one's esteem.
senses.whyCN: prae- 意为「在前」，ferre 意为「搬运」，被喜欢的那样东西于是被搬到另一样东西前面，排在心上更靠前的位置。

senses.title: Choose one option rather than the other
senses.definition: to choose one course or option rather than another because it suits one better
senses.definitionCN: 因为更合心意而选择一种做法或选项，而不是另一种
senses.example: We preferred to walk rather than wait for the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们宁愿走路，也不想等公交。
senses.why: Once one thing is placed in front, the hand follows it, so preference turns into a choice between courses of action.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西一旦被放到前面，手就会跟着它走，于是「更喜欢」变成了在几种做法之间的选择。

senses.title: Give precedence to a claim or method
senses.titleCN: 给予某项主张或方法优先地位
senses.definition: to treat one claim, method or person as more important than the others
senses.definitionCN: 把某项主张、方法或某个人看得比其他更重
senses.example: The committee preferred the cheaper design.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会更倾向于那个造价更低的方案。
senses.why: Ranking is placing in a row, and what is carried to the front of the row is what counts first.
senses.whyCN: 排序就是把东西排成一列，被搬到最前面的那一个，就是最先被考虑的那一个。

senses.title: Bring a charge or claim before a court
senses.titleCN: 向法庭提出控告或主张
senses.definition: to bring a charge, claim or request formally before a court or an authority
senses.definitionCN: 正式向法庭或主管机关提出控告、索赔或请求
senses.example: The prosecutor preferred charges of fraud against the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官对这家公司提出了欺诈指控。
senses.why: Legal Latin kept the literal sense of bringing something forward, so a charge is carried before the bench.
senses.whyCN: 法律拉丁语保留了「把东西搬到前面」的字面意思，因此控告就是被搬到法官席前的东西。

senses.title: Advance someone to a higher office
senses.titleCN: 把某人提拔到更高的职位
senses.definition: to promote someone to a higher position or a more valuable office
senses.definitionCN: 把某人提升到更高或更优厚的职位
senses.example: The bishop was preferred to a wealthier see.
senses.exampleCN: 这位主教被提拔到一个更富裕的教区。
senses.why: A person raised above his peers is literally carried in front of them in rank.
senses.whyCN: 一个人被抬到同辈之上，在位次上就是被搬到了他们前面。

senses.title: Regard one explanation as more likely
senses.titleCN: 认为某一种解释更可能成立
senses.definition: to judge one explanation, reading or hypothesis as more likely than another
senses.definitionCN: 判断某一种解释、读法或假说比另一种更可能
senses.example: Historians prefer the simpler reading of the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家更认可对这封信较为简单的解读。
senses.why: The mind also carries things forward: among competing readings, one is placed ahead of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 心思也会搬东西：在几种相互竞争的解释里，总有一种被放到其余之前。

senses.title: Express a softer wish about another person's action
senses.titleCN: 委婉表达希望对方如何做
senses.definition: to say politely that one would rather have something done in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地表示自己更希望某事以某种方式进行
senses.example: I would prefer it if you called before coming.
senses.exampleCN: 我希望你来之前先打个电话。
senses.why: The comparative force softens a request: the speaker names a preferred arrangement instead of giving an order.
senses.whyCN: 比较的意味让请求变软：说话人只是说出更合意的安排，而不是下命令。

senses.title: Decide at one's own discretion
senses.titleCN: 按自己的判断自行决定
senses.definition: to decide according to one's own judgment, especially in formal rules that leave the choice open
senses.definitionCN: 按自己的判断作出决定，尤用于把选择权留给当事人的正式规则
senses.example: The trustee may, as he prefers, sell the land at auction.
senses.exampleCN: 受托人可以按自己的判断，以拍卖方式出售这块土地。
senses.why: The oldest sense of placing one thing before another survives as the freedom to put whichever course one likes first.
senses.whyCN: 「把某样东西放到前面」这个最古老的意思，在这里留存为「可以把中意的做法排在前面」的自由。

intro.en: Prefer comes through Old French from Latin praeferre, built on prae- meaning before and ferre meaning to carry or bear. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: prefer 经古法语来自拉丁语 praeferre，由 prae-「在前」与 ferre「搬运、承载」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry or bear, and its past participle latus stands behind English words such as relate and translate. Its older source is generally reconstructed as a root meaning to carry.
items.cn: ferre 意为「搬运、承载」，其过去分词 latus 支撑着 relate、translate 等英语词。它更早的来源通常被重构为一个表示「搬运」的词根。

items.en: Prae- meaning before plus ferre produced praeferre, to place or carry in front, and by extension to value one thing above another.
items.cn: 表示「在前」的 prae- 加 ferre 构成 praeferre，意为「放到前面、搬在前面」，并引申为把某物看得比另一物更重。

items.en: Old French preferer brought the verb into English in the late fourteenth century, at first in the sense of putting a person or thing before others.
items.cn: 古法语 preferer 在十四世纪后期把这个动词带入英语，最初指把人或物放到其他之前。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the verb named esteeming one thing above another, and legal usage used it for bringing a charge or request forward.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个动词已指看重某物胜过另一物，法律用语则用它表示把控告或请求呈到前面。

items.en: The everyday sense of liking one thing better than another settled in ordinary speech, while the legal and church senses stayed in specialized use.
items.cn: 「更喜欢某物」这一日常义在普通口语中固定下来，而法律与教会用语里的意思则留在专门场合。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English citation is not fixed, and the deeper Indo-European root of ferre is a reconstructed form rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语中最早的书证年代没有定论；ferre 更深的印欧语词根属重构形式，并非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb ferre but differs in prefix; the second holds words for liking and picking that are close in use. One look-alike has a different origin.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁动词 ferre，只是前缀不同；第二组是用法相近的「喜爱、挑选」类词。其中有一个形似词来源不同。

entries.definition: Re- meaning back plus ferre: to carry a matter back to a source, hence to direct attention or consult.
entries.definitionCN: re-「向后」加 ferre：把某事带回源头，因而指指向某处或查阅。

entries.definition: Con- meaning together plus ferre: to bring matters together, hence to consult or to bestow.
entries.definitionCN: con-「共同」加 ferre：把事情带到一处，因而指商议或授予。

entries.definition: Dis- meaning apart plus ferre: to carry things in different directions, hence to be unlike.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「分开」加 ferre：把东西带向不同方向，因而指彼此不同。

entries.definition: From Old French poroffrir, built on offrir and Latin offerre meaning to bring before; it looks like prefer but the prefix and source differ.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 poroffrir，由 offrir 与拉丁语 offerre「呈到面前」构成；它与 prefer 形似，但前缀与来源都不同。

entries.definition: To treat one person or option with special approval; it stresses approval rather than a comparison between two things.
entries.definitionCN: 带着特别的认可对待某个人或某种选项；它强调认可，而不是两物之间的比较。

entries.definition: To pick one option; prefer names the leaning, choose names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 挑出一个选项；prefer 命名的是倾向，choose 命名的是动作。

entries.definition: To make a choice, often in a formal or deliberate context; it does not carry the comparative force of liking one more than another.
entries.definitionCN: 作出选择，常用于正式或慎重的场合；它不带有「比另一物更喜欢」的比较意味。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for finding something pleasant; prefer adds a comparison with something else.
entries.definitionCN: 表示觉得某物令人愉快的日常动词；prefer 则加上了与另一物的比较。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real root, the real family and the phrases the verb keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、真实的词根、真实的同族词，以及这个动词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: prae- meaning before plus ferre meaning carry: to carry one thing in front of another.
normal.cn: prae-「在前」加 ferre「搬运」：把一样东西搬到另一样前面。

normal.en: The family runs prefer, preference, preferable, preferably, preferential and preferment.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 prefer（更喜欢）、preference（偏好）、preferable（更可取的）、preferably（更可取地）、preferential（优先的）、preferment（提拔）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the comparison: prefer tea to coffee, prefer to wait, strongly prefer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出比较关系：喜欢茶胜过咖啡、宁愿等待、强烈偏好。

normal.en: The same root runs through refer, confer, differ, infer and transfer, each with its own prefix.
normal.cn: 同一词根贯穿 refer、confer、differ、infer、transfer，各自配上不同的前缀。

normal.en: Legal usage keeps the old forward motion: to prefer charges is to bring them before a court.
normal.cn: 法律用法保住旧的「向前搬」动作：提出控告就是把控告呈到法庭前。

abstract.en: Picture two doors and a hand already resting on the right handle.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇门，一只手已经按在右边那扇的把手上。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk placing one file on top of a stack.
abstract.cn: 想象一名职员把一份卷宗放到整叠文件的最上面。

abstract.en: Picture a compass needle that always settles a little east of north.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚罗盘针，每次都停在正北略偏东的位置。

examples.en: Most readers prefer the shorter edition.
examples.cn: 多数读者更喜欢篇幅较短的版本。

examples.en: She preferred to say nothing until the facts were clear.
examples.cn: 在事实清楚之前，她宁愿什么都不说。

examples.en: The court preferred charges against two officers.
examples.cn: 法庭对两名警官提出了指控。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞佛」——先把喜欢的那件捧到前面 → prefer 更喜欢、宁愿

root: 拉丁 praeferre「放到前面、看重」= prae-「在前」+ ferre「搬运、承载」；ferre 的印欧语来源通常被重构为表示「搬运」的词根。英语 prefer 经古法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: one thing is carried in front of another, and that placement is applied to taste, action, ranking, legal charges, offices, explanations, polite wishes and finally to open discretion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把一样东西搬到另一样前面，这个摆放再依次用于口味、行动、排序、法律控告、职位、解释、礼貌愿望，最后用于留有余地的自行裁量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two things offered side by side, and one is carried to the front of the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样东西并排摆在面前，其中一样被搬到手上更靠前的位置。

branches.en: TASTE AND ACTION: the thing carried to the front is first liked, then taken.
branches.cn: 口味与行动：被搬到前面的东西先被喜欢，再被拿走。

branches.en: RANKING: precedence is the same placement seen as order rather than desire.
branches.cn: 排序：优先地位是同一种摆放，只是被看成次序而非喜好。

branches.en: FORMAL FORWARDING: a charge or a candidate is brought before the bench or above one's peers.
branches.cn: 正式呈交：控告或人选被带到法官席前，或被抬到同辈之上。

branches.en: READING: among explanations the mind puts one ahead of the rest.
branches.cn: 解读：在几种解释中，心思把其中一种放到其余之前。

branches.en: SOFTENED WILL: a polite wish and a formal discretion both leave the preferred course to the speaker.
branches.cn: 柔化的意愿：礼貌的愿望与正式的裁量，都把中意的做法留给说话人自己。

intro.en: Prefer can be read from a Latin prefix and a Latin verb that also build a large English family.
intro.cn: prefer 可以按一个拉丁前缀与一个拉丁动词逐段读出，这两部分还构成一大族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ferre gives refer, confer, differ, infer, transfer and prefer; prae- adds the sense of being in front.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ferre 衍生 refer、confer、differ、infer、transfer 与 prefer；prae- 加上「在前面」的意思。

items.example: The prefix also appears in predict and precede.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀也出现在 predict（预测）与 precede（在……之前）里。

items.example: Its participle latus underlies translate and relate.
items.exampleCN: 它的过去分词 latus 是 translate 与 relate 的词源基础。

items.meaning: to carry in front, hence to value more
items.exampleCN: 她更喜欢早一班的那趟车。

items.meaning: the state of liking one thing more
items.meaningCN: 偏好；更喜爱某物的状态
items.example: Her preference for quiet rooms is well known.
items.exampleCN: 她偏爱安静的房间，这是众所皆知的。

items.example: The earlier flight is preferable in winter.
items.exampleCN: 冬天早一班的航班更可取。

items.meaning: if the choice were open, in the better way
items.example: Bring cash, preferably in small notes.
items.exampleCN: 带上现金，最好是小面额的。

items.meaningCN: 优先的；给予一方优待的

items.meaning: an advance to a higher post
items.example: His preferment came after years of service.
items.exampleCN: 他在多年任职之后获得提拔。

items.structure: pro- + offerre (to bring before), a different formation
items.meaning: to hold out something for acceptance
items.exampleCN: 她递上一张手写的便条。

derivatives.structure: prefer + -ence (state) → the state of holding one thing above another
derivatives.meaning: a greater liking for one thing

derivatives.structure: prefer + -able (fit to be chosen) → fit to be chosen rather than the other
preferable + -ly (adverb) → in the more desirable way
prefer + -ential (relational adjective) → marked by giving advantage to one side
prefer + -ment (result) → the result of being raised above others

definition_zh: 更可取的；较好的；更合意的；更适宜的
definition_en: better or more suitable than another choice, especially when two or more options are being compared
core_image: 天平两端各放一份方案，一端缓缓下沉，指针偏向那一边
scene: 两份方案摊在桌上，众人讨论到深夜，最后目光都落到右边那一份。For a small team, a simple plan is usually preferable to a clever one.
sceneCN: 这里 preferable 是「更可取的」（第 1 个义项：两相比较中更值得选择）；句意为对小团队来说，简单的方案通常比巧妙的方案更可取。图中可辨识物件：桌面、两份方案、天平指针。

pos.zh: 更可取的；较好的；更合意的；更适宜的

derivatives.zh: 同一拉丁词干上的动词，经古法语 preferer 进入英语，义为「更喜欢；宁愿」
由 prefer 加名词后缀 -ence 构成，义为「偏爱；优先权」
由 preferable 加 -ly 构成，义为「最好；更合意地」

senses.title: Better when two things are compared
senses.definition: better or more suitable than the other option in a direct comparison
senses.definitionCN: 在两个选项直接比较时，比另一个更好或更合适
senses.example: A quiet room is preferable to a noisy one for study.
senses.exampleCN: 学习时，安静的房间比喧闹的房间更可取。
senses.why: Latin praeferre meant to carry one thing in front of another, so the adjective starts from a ranking in which one choice is set ahead of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praeferre 意为把一物抬到另一物前面，所以这个形容词的起点是排位：有一个选择被摆到了其余选择之前。

senses.title: More agreeable to a particular person
senses.definition: more to someone's liking, so that the person would choose it if left free to do so
senses.definitionCN: 更合乎某人的心意，若由他自由选择就会选它
senses.example: For her, an early flight is preferable to a late one.
senses.exampleCN: 对她来说，早班飞机比晚班飞机更合意。
senses.why: Preference is personal, so once the word ranks options it can also describe what one person happens to like better, not only what is better in general.
senses.whyCN: 偏爱是个人化的，所以这个词一旦用来给选项排位，也就能描述某个人恰好更喜欢什么，而不只是客观上什么更好。

senses.title: Wiser in the circumstances
senses.definition: more sensible or advisable in a particular situation, all things considered
senses.definitionCN: 通盘考虑之后，在特定情形里更明智、更值得采纳
senses.example: Given the ice on the road, walking is preferable to driving tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 考虑到路面结冰，今晚走路比开车更明智。
senses.why: When the circumstances are brought in, the comparison stops being a matter of taste and becomes a judgement about safety or good sense, which is how the word reaches advice.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把具体情形带进来，比较就不再是口味问题，而变成对安全与否、明智与否的判断，这个词也由此进入劝告的语境。

intro.en: Preferable joins a Latin prefix meaning before to a verb meaning to carry, and reached English through French as the adjective built on prefer.
intro.cn: preferable 把一个意为「在前」的拉丁前缀与一个意为「携带」的动词连在一起，经法语作为 prefer 的形容词进入英语。

items.en: The root behind Latin ferre is usually reconstructed as bher-, meaning to carry; it is a reconstructed form, not a word found in any text.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语 ferre 背后的词根可重构为 bher-，意为「携带」；这只是重构形式，并非任何文本中出现的词。

items.en: Ferre meant to bear or to carry, and it built a large family of verbs about bringing, holding and offering.
items.cn: ferre 意为承载、携带，由此造出一大批表示带来、持有与呈递的动词。

items.en: Prae- meant in front or before, so praeferre first meant to carry something in front, then to set one thing above another.
items.cn: prae- 意为在前面或之前，praeferre 先指把某物抬到前面，再引申为把一物置于另一物之上。

items.en: Old French kept the verb as preferer, meaning to put first or to value more, and formed the adjective preferable from it.
items.cn: 古法语把动词保留为 preferer，意为置于首位或更看重，并由它造出形容词 preferable。

items.en: English borrowed both prefer and preferable, and the adjective settled into the pattern preferable to, naming the better of two choices.
items.cn: 英语同时借入 prefer 与 preferable，这个形容词后来固定在 preferable to 的结构里，指两个选择中更好的那个。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin verb ferre; the near-meaning group gathers words that also rank one thing above another.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁动词 ferre 上的形式；近义组收同样把一物排在另一物之上的词。

entries.definition: To like one thing more than another and choose it.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的动词，义为更喜欢并选择某物。

entries.definition: The act of liking one thing more, or the thing that is liked more.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的名词，指偏爱这一行为，或所偏爱的事物。

entries.definition: If possible, as the more desirable choice.
entries.definitionCN: 由 preferable 加 -ly 构成，义为「最好；更合意地」。

entries.definition: Promotion to a higher position, from the older sense of being put forward.
entries.definitionCN: 由 prefer 加 -ment 构成，指晋升，来自「被推到前面」的旧义。

entries.definition: Of higher quality or more suitable than something else.
entries.definitionCN: 更好的；质量更高或更合适的。

entries.definition: Worth wanting or choosing because it brings an advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 值得向往的；因有好处而值得选择的。

entries.definition: Sensible and likely to bring a good result.
entries.definitionCN: 明智的；很可能带来好结果的。

entries.definition: Better than another thing of the same kind.
entries.definitionCN: 优于同类其他事物的；更好的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of carrying with a prefix meaning before, and its family keeps returning to ranking, liking and choosing.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是带「在前」前缀的拉丁「携带」动词，同族词反复回到排位、偏爱与选择。

normal.en: Praeferre is prae- plus ferre, to carry before, so to prefer is to put one thing ahead of another in your mind.
normal.cn: praeferre 是 prae- 加 ferre（携带），意为抬到前面，所以 to prefer 就是在心里把一物排到另一物之前。

normal.en: Preferable adds -able to the same stem, so it means worth being put first.
normal.cn: preferable 在同一词干后加 -able，意为「值得被放在前面的」。

normal.en: The fixed pattern is preferable to, not preferable than, because the Latin prefix already carries the comparison.
normal.cn: 固定说法是 preferable to 而不是 preferable than，因为比较的意思已由这个词本身承担。

normal.en: Preference is the noun of the same family, naming the state of liking one thing more.
normal.cn: preference 是同族名词，指更喜欢某物这种状态。

normal.en: Preferably is the adverb, used when a wish is stated politely rather than as an order.
normal.cn: preferably 是副词，用于客气地说出愿望，而不是下达命令。

abstract.en: To call something preferable is to admit that both options exist and that one has been weighed against the other.
abstract.cn: 说某物更可取，就是承认两个选项都存在，而且其中一个已经被拿来与另一个掂量过。

abstract.en: The word does not say the other choice is bad; it only says this one stands in front.
abstract.cn: 这个词并没有说另一个选择不好，只说这一个站到了前面。

abstract.en: Every preference is a small act of ordering the world, and the adjective names the result of that act.
abstract.cn: 每一次偏爱都是给世界排一次小序，这个形容词命名的正是排序的结果。

examples.en: For a small team, a simple plan is usually preferable to a clever one.
examples.cn: 对小团队来说，简单的方案通常比巧妙的方案更可取。

examples.en: Given the ice on the road, walking is preferable to driving tonight.
examples.cn: 考虑到路面结冰，今晚走路比开车更明智。

examples.en: Most parents find a short walk to school preferable to a long bus ride.
examples.cn: 多数家长觉得走一小段路去学校比坐长途公交更合意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偏爱若宝」——偏爱的东西总被当成宝贝放在最前面；preferable 就是更可取的。

root: 由拉丁语前缀 prae-（在前）与动词 ferre（携带）构成 praeferre（置于前面、更看重），经古法语 preferer 及形容词 preferable 进入英语；同族词有 prefer、preference、preferment。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a choice set in front of the others; the senses divide into an objective comparison, a personal liking, and a judgement about what is wise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被摆到其他选项之前的选择；义项由此分出客观比较、个人偏爱，以及对是否明智的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two plans on a scale, one side sinking slowly as the needle leans toward it.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两端各放一份方案，一端缓缓下沉，指针偏向那一边。

branches.en: a hand moving one sheet of paper to the top of a pile
branches.cn: 一只手把一张纸移到一叠纸的最上面

branches.en: a traveller choosing the earlier of two trains
branches.cn: 旅客在两班车中选了较早的一班

branches.en: a sign turning walkers away from an icy slope
branches.cn: 一块牌子让行人避开结冰的坡道

branches.en: two menus laid side by side on a table
branches.cn: 两份菜单并排摊在桌上

branches.en: a family voting on where to eat
branches.cn: 一家人投票决定去哪儿吃饭

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin prefix of place, a verb of carrying, and an English suffix meaning worth being chosen.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀、表示携带的动词，以及一个意为「值得被选」的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Preferable rests on Latin praeferre, to carry before, built from prae- and ferre; French reshaped it into preferer and its adjective.
latinIntro.cn: preferable 立足于拉丁语 praeferre（抬到前面），由 prae- 与 ferre 构成；法语把它改写为 preferer 及其形容词。

items.meaning: to put first, to value more

definition_zh: 偏爱；优先；优待；优先权
definition_en: the choosing of one thing over another, or the right to be served or paid before others
core_image: 一只盘子里的两块点心本一模一样，拿筷子的人却每次都先夹靠左那一块，动作快得像是早已决定
scene: 早上七点，车站售票窗口前拉起了两列队伍，戴徽章的工作人员把一侧的人先引到柜台前。Give your preference to families with small children when seats are limited.
sceneCN: 这里本词指优先安排或优先照顾（第 2 个义项：把先办、先得的次序给别人）；句意为座位有限时优先安排带幼儿的家庭；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 偏爱；更喜欢的事物（可数或不可数）
优先；优先权（不可数）
（贸易或关税上的）优惠待遇

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀，回到同族动词，语义偏移为「更喜欢；宁愿」
由本词加表关系的形容词后缀构成，语义偏移为「优先的；优待的」
由同族形容词加表方式的副词后缀构成，语义偏移为「最好是」
由同族动词加表「可……的」后缀构成，语义偏移为「更可取的」
由本词加表股份的名词构成，语义偏移为「优先股」

senses.title: Liking one thing more
senses.definition: a stronger liking for one thing than for another
senses.definitionCN: 对某物的喜欢超过对另一物的喜欢
senses.example: Her preference is for strong tea rather than coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 她偏爱浓茶而非咖啡。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to carry a thing in front; what is put in front is what one favours.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为把某物搬到前面；被放到前面，就是被偏爱的。

senses.title: The right to be served first
senses.definition: the right or practice of being dealt with before others
senses.definitionCN: 先于他人得到办理或照顾的权利或做法
senses.example: Give your preference to families with small children when seats are limited.
senses.exampleCN: 座位有限时优先安排带幼儿的家庭。
senses.why: Being placed before others is a literal carrying forward, so the noun marks rank as well as taste.
senses.whyCN: 被放在他人之前，正是字面意义上的搬到前面，因此该名词也标出次序。

senses.title: A trade advantage
senses.definition: a lower tariff or easier terms granted to certain trading partners
senses.definitionCN: 给予某些贸易伙伴的较低关税或更宽条件
senses.example: The agreement grants tariff preference to the smallest exporters.
senses.exampleCN: 该协议给予最小规模的出口商关税优惠。
senses.why: A partner carried to the front of the queue is a partner who pays less at the border.
senses.whyCN: 被提到队伍前面的伙伴，就是在关境上付款更少的伙伴。

senses.title: A first claim in law
senses.definition: the right of one creditor to be paid before others from a debtor's property
senses.definitionCN: 某一债权人从债务人财产中先于他人受偿的权利
senses.example: The bank's preference over the land was recorded at the registry.
senses.exampleCN: 银行对这块地的优先受偿权已在登记处记录。
senses.why: Law keeps the order of payment literal: one claim is carried ahead of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 法律把付款次序说得很字面：一项债权被搬到其余债权之前。

senses.title: One's first choice
senses.definition: the person or thing one would choose first if only one could be had
senses.definitionCN: 若只能得到一个，会最先选择的人或物
senses.example: This route is our preference for the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路线是我们过河的首选。
senses.why: Choosing is ranking, and the top of the ranking is what stands in front.
senses.whyCN: 选择就是排序，排在最前面的那一个就是被放到前面的。

senses.title: Settings stored by software
senses.definition: stored choices that tell a program how its user wants it to behave
senses.definitionCN: 程序记录下来的、说明用户希望它如何运作的选择
senses.example: The app keeps your preference even after you sign out.
senses.exampleCN: 即使退出登录，这款应用仍保留你的偏好设置。
senses.why: A machine that remembers a choice keeps a small record of what its user put first.
senses.whyCN: 会记住选择机器，就是留下用户「把什么放在前面」的小记录。

senses.title: A pattern in buying
senses.definition: the tendency of buyers to favour certain goods, brands or features
senses.definitionCN: 购买者更偏爱某些商品、品牌或特性的趋势
senses.example: Surveys track preference for local produce.
senses.exampleCN: 调查追踪消费者对本地农产品的偏好。
senses.why: Economists widen one person's taste into a measurable pattern of favouring.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把一个人的口味扩展成可测量的偏爱模式。

senses.title: A taste shaped by culture
senses.definition: a leaning in style, art or custom that a group learns rather than inherits
senses.definitionCN: 群体习得而非天生继承的风格、艺术或习俗上的偏向
senses.example: Colour preference varies sharply between regions.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色偏好在不同地区差别很大。
senses.why: Shared leaning is still a carrying forward of one option, only now by a whole group.
senses.whyCN: 共享的偏向仍然是「把某一选项搬到前面」，只是搬运者换成了一个群体。

intro.en: Preference comes from Latin praeferre 'to carry in front, place before', built from prae- 'before' and ferre 'to carry'; English took it through French.
intro.cn: 本词来自拉丁语 praeferre「搬到前面、置于前面」，由表「在前」的前缀加 ferre「携带」构成；英语经法语借入。

items.en: Ferre meant 'to carry, bear, bring', one of the most common verbs of movement in Latin.
items.cn: ferre 意为「携带、承载、带来」，是拉丁语中最常见的移动动词之一。

items.en: Prae- meant 'before, in front', whether of place or of rank.
items.cn: 表「在前」的前缀意为在位置上或次序上靠前。

items.en: Praeferre joined the two: to carry something in front of something else, hence to set one above another.
items.cn: 两相结合构成的动词意为把某物搬到另一物之前，因此引申为把某物排到另一物之上。

items.en: French made a noun of the verb, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century for the act of favouring.
items.cn: 法语把该动词名词化，英语在十四世纪借入，指偏爱的行为。

items.en: Courts and merchants narrowed the noun to a right of first payment and a lower tariff.
items.cn: 法庭与商人把该名词收窄为先受偿的权利与更低的关税。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the earliest English use is placed in the fourteenth century, and the older base behind ferre is generally considered a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：英语最早书证定于十四世纪，而 ferre 背后的更早词基一般认为是重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close and are often confused with this noun; group two holds words for choosing and for liking.
note.cn: 第一组是与本词形近或音近、常被混淆的词；第二组是表示选择与喜爱的词。

entries.definition: The base verb meaning to like one thing better; the noun adds the result of that liking.
entries.definitionCN: 基干动词，意为更喜欢某物；名词则加出这种喜爱的结果。

entries.definition: The adjective built on this noun, describing treatment that gives someone first place.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词构成的形容词，描述给予某人优先地位的处理方式。

entries.definition: A noun for advancement in office, from the same verb but with a different sense.
entries.definitionCN: 同出该动词，但指职位上的升迁，义项不同。

entries.definition: An adjective saying one option is better; it evaluates rather than records a taste.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，表示某个选项更好；它作评价，而不记录口味。

entries.definition: The act of picking or the set of options; preference is the leaning that guides the pick.
entries.definitionCN: 挑选的动作或可选范围；本词是引导挑选的那种偏向。

entries.definition: Simple fondness for something, without the sense of ranking one above another.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物的朴素喜爱，不含把某物排在另一物之上的意味。

entries.definition: The state of coming first because of urgency or importance, a matter of order rather than taste.
entries.definitionCN: 因紧急或重要而排在最前，讲的是次序而非口味。

entries.definition: A favourable condition or benefit; the trade sense of preference is one kind of advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 有利条件或好处；本词的贸易义是其中一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Two real parts: a prefix meaning before, and a verb meaning to carry.
normal.cn: 两个真实成分：一个表「在前」的前缀，加一个表「携带」的动词。

normal.en: The family runs prefer, preference, preferable, preferably, preferential.
normal.cn: 同族词包括更喜欢、偏爱、更可取的、最好是、优先的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: have a preference for, give preference to, in preference to.
normal.cn: 固定说法：偏爱、优先考虑、优先于。

normal.en: Every technical use puts somebody at the front: a creditor, an exporter, a passenger, a setting.
normal.cn: 每个专业用法都把某一方放到前面：债权人、出口商、乘客、某项设置。

normal.en: The noun records a ranking; the verb records the act of ranking.
normal.cn: 名词记录的是排序结果，动词记录的是排序的动作。

abstract.en: Picture two identical cakes on a plate and a hand that always reaches left first.
abstract.cn: 想象盘里两块一模一样的点心，一只手每次都先伸向左边。

abstract.en: Picture a rope laid across a queue to mark who is let through first.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绳子横在队伍中，标出谁先被放行。

abstract.en: Picture a screen that remembers which button you press every morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一块屏幕记住了你每天早上按的那个按钮。

examples.en: He has a strong preference for quiet rooms.
examples.cn: 他非常偏爱安静的房间。

examples.en: Preference was given to applicants from the region.
examples.cn: 优先考虑了来自本地区的申请人。

examples.en: You can change your preference at any time.
examples.cn: 你随时可以更改自己的偏好设置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「在前」与「携带」合起来看：把某样东西搬到前面，就是偏爱它、优先待它。

root: 拉丁 praeferre「搬到前面、置于前面」＝表「在前」的前缀＋ferre「携带」；英语经法语借入，由「置于前」引申为偏爱与优先；更深词基一般认为是重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one move: an object carried to the front is the one liked, served first, taxed less, paid first, chosen first, remembered by a machine, favoured by buyers and shaped by a culture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：被搬到前面的东西，就是被偏爱的、先被服务的、少缴税的、先受偿的、首选中的、被机器记住的、被买家青睐的、被文化塑造的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two identical cakes on a plate, and a hand that always reaches for the left one first.
core.cn: 核心意象：盘里两块一模一样的点心，一只手每次都先伸向左边的。

branches.en: TASTE AND CULTURE: one person's liking and a region's shared style are the same favouring at two scales.
branches.cn: 口味与文化：一个人的喜爱与一个地区共享的风格，是同一种偏爱在两个尺度上。

branches.en: RANK AND TRADE: being served before others and paying less at the border both mean being moved ahead.
branches.cn: 次序与贸易：先被服务与在关境少缴税，都意味着被移到前面。

branches.en: THE LEGAL CLAIM: a creditor carried ahead of the rest keeps the image in strict order.
branches.cn: 法律的求偿：被搬到其余人之前的债权人，把这意象保持在严格次序里。

branches.en: THE FIRST CHOICE: what one would pick first stands at the head of a ranking.
branches.cn: 首选：最先会挑的那个，排在名单的最前。

branches.en: MACHINE AND MARKET: a stored setting and a buyer's pattern both record what is put first.
branches.cn: 机器与市场：存下的设置与买家的模式，都记录「什么被放在前面」。

intro.en: Preference is a Latin noun formed from a prefix, a carrying verb and a noun suffix; the same pieces build a small English family, so the word can be read in parts.
intro.cn: 本词是由表方向的前缀、表「携带」的动词与名词后缀构成的拉丁名词；同样的部件构成一个小英语词族，可按部分读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- supplies 'before' and ferre supplies 'carry'; the noun suffix names the act, and English adds nothing further.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表「在前」的前缀提供「之前」之义，表「携带」的动词提供搬运义，名词后缀命名这一行为；英语不再加缀。

items.example: The verb is the carrying itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词就是「搬」这个动作本身。

items.meaning: to carry in front, to set above
items.example: To carry a thing in front is to give it the first place.
items.exampleCN: 把东西搬到前面，就是给它第一位。

items.example: The state noun named the favouring.
items.exampleCN: 这个状态名词命名偏爱。

items.meaning: a liking, or a right to come first
items.example: Her preference is for the coast road.
Bring a map, preferably a paper one.
items.exampleCN: 带张地图，最好是纸质的。
这家公司赢得了优待条件。

items.meaning: a share paid before ordinary shares

definition_zh: 怀孕的；意味深长的；充满……的；孕育着……的
definition_en: carrying a baby inside the body, or full of meaning, feeling or possibility that has not yet shown itself
core_image: 一位妇人一手扶着腰，低头看向自己微微隆起的腹部
scene: 候诊室的长椅上，她把手放在小腹上，等护士叫号。The doctor told her she was pregnant with twins.
sceneCN: 这里 pregnant 是「怀孕的」（第 1 个义项：体内怀有胎儿）；句意为医生告诉她怀的是双胞胎。图中可辨识物件：长椅、候诊室、扶着腹部的手。

pos.zh: 怀孕的；意味深长的；充满……的；孕育着……的

derivatives.zh: 由 pregnant 换后缀 -cy 构成，义为「怀孕；孕期」
由前缀 im- 加拉丁词干 pregnant- 构成，义为「使怀孕；使充满」

senses.title: Carrying a child in the body
senses.definition: having a baby or other young growing inside the body
senses.definitionCN: 体内怀有胎儿或幼崽，正在发育
senses.example: She was pregnant with her second child.
senses.exampleCN: 她怀着第二个孩子。
senses.why: Latin praegnans joins prae-, before, with a root for being born, so the word pictures a child who is already there before it arrives.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praegnans 把表示「在前」的 prae- 与表示出生的词根合在一起，画面是孩子还没降生就已经在那里了。

senses.title: Heavy with meaning that is left unsaid
senses.definition: of a pause, look or remark, so full of meaning that everyone notices what is not said
senses.definitionCN: 指停顿、眼神或话语含义极满，旁人都察觉到没说出口的部分
senses.example: He let a pregnant pause hang in the air before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 他先让一阵意味深长的停顿悬在空中，然后才回答。
senses.why: A pause that seems to carry something not yet spoken borrows the image of a body holding a hidden life, so the silence looks ready to give birth to a word.
senses.whyCN: 一个仿佛藏着未说之语的停顿，借用了身体怀着一个隐秘生命的画面，于是沉默看上去随时会生出一句话。

senses.title: Full of something about to happen
senses.definition: holding a great deal of a quality or possibility that has not yet come out
senses.definitionCN: 含有大量尚未显现的性质或可能性
senses.example: The old harbour is pregnant with possibility.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧港口孕育着各种可能。
senses.why: If a body can hold a new life, then anything holding a future can be called pregnant with it, and the preposition with marks what is being carried inside.
senses.whyCN: 身体既然能怀着新生命，任何含着未来的事物也就能说成 pregnant with，介词 with 标出的正是里面所怀的东西。

senses.title: Fertile in invention, of a mind or remark
senses.definition: of a mind or a remark, full of ideas and quick to produce them
senses.definitionCN: 指头脑或言辞充满想法，随时能生出新东西
senses.example: Her pregnant wit turned a dull meeting into a debate.
senses.exampleCN: 她机敏的才智把一场沉闷的会议变成了辩论。
senses.why: The oldest figurative use praises a mind that is full and ready to give birth to ideas, a sense now mostly found in literary writing.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的比喻用法赞美一颗饱满、随时能生出想法的头脑，这层意思如今多见于文学性的文字。

intro.en: Pregnant comes from a Latin adjective that puts before together with a root for birth, and English took it through French with both the bodily and the figurative senses.
intro.cn: pregnant 出自一个把「在前」与「出生」词根合起来的拉丁形容词，英语经法语借入时同时带来了身体义与比喻义。

items.en: The root behind the Latin word for giving birth is usually reconstructed as gen-, meaning to beget; it is a reconstruction, not a word recorded in any text.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语中表示生育的词根可重构为 gen-，意为「生育」；这只是重构形式，并非任何文本里出现过的词。

items.en: Praegnans combined prae-, before, with that root, describing a woman whose child is already there before the birth.
items.cn: praegnans 由表示「在前」的 prae- 与上述词根合成，形容女子在分娩之前就已经怀着孩子。

items.en: The stem pregnant- supplied the cases used in running prose, and it is the shape that passed into French and then English.
items.cn: 词干 pregnant- 提供了行文中使用的各个格形式，也正是传入法语、再传入英语的形状。

items.en: Old French used the word for a woman with child and also for a remark heavy with meaning.
items.cn: 古法语既用这个词指怀着孩子的妇人，也用来形容含义沉重的话语。

items.en: English kept both branches, so a woman and a pause can be pregnant, and pregnant with extends the image to anything full of a future.
items.cn: 英语保留了两条分支，于是妇人与停顿都可以是 pregnant，而 pregnant with 把这一意象扩展到任何充满未来之物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin stem for pregnancy; the near-meaning group gathers words for expecting a child and for meaning held back.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁「怀孕」词干上的形式；近义组收表示期待孩子与含义未尽之物的词。

entries.definition: The state or period of carrying a child in the body.
entries.definitionCN: 由 pregnant 转成的名词，指怀孕的状态或孕期。

entries.definition: To make someone pregnant, or to fill something through and through.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的动词，义为使怀孕，或使某物充满。

entries.definition: Relating to the period before birth; it only shares the prefix prae-, and its second element comes from a different Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 产前的；只是前缀与目标词相近，后半部分来自另一个拉丁词，词源不同。

entries.definition: Waiting for a baby to be born, used of a mother or a family.
entries.definitionCN: 待产的；指母亲或家庭正等待孩子出生。

entries.definition: Carrying eggs or young, the technical word used in biology.
entries.definitionCN: 怀卵的；怀胎的，生物学使用的专业词。

entries.definition: Having a serious or important meaning that is easy to feel.
entries.definitionCN: 有意义的；含有严肃或重要意味的。

entries.definition: Hinting at something without saying it directly.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示的；不直说而让人想到某事的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of carrying a child, and its family keeps returning to hidden life, withheld meaning and stored possibility.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「怀着孩子」的形容词，同族词反复回到隐秘的生命、未尽的意思与储存的可能。

normal.en: Praegnans is prae- plus a birth root, so the word literally places the child before the birth.
normal.cn: praegnans 是 prae- 加表示出生的词根，字面上就是把孩子放在分娩之前。

normal.en: The stem pregnant- carries the meaning through French, and English added no new root of its own.
normal.cn: 词干 pregnant- 把含义一路带到法语，英语没有再添加自己的词根。

normal.en: Pregnant with is the fixed pattern for the figurative sense, as in pregnant with possibility.
normal.cn: pregnant with 是比喻义的固定结构，如 pregnant with possibility。

normal.en: Pregnancy replaces the adjective ending with -cy to name the state rather than the person.
normal.cn: pregnancy 用 -cy 替换形容词词尾，用来指状态而不是人。

normal.en: Impregnate adds im- and shifts the word to the act of filling, whether with a child or with a quality.
normal.cn: impregnate 加 im-，把词义转向「使充满」的动作，充入的可以是孩子，也可以是某种性质。

abstract.en: A pregnant pause and a pregnant woman share one picture: something is inside, alive, and not yet shown.
abstract.cn: 意味深长的停顿与怀孕的妇人共用一幅画面：里面有东西活着，但还没露面。

abstract.en: The word treats the future as something already carried rather than something still to come.
abstract.cn: 这个词把未来当成已经怀在身上的东西，而不是尚未到来的东西。

abstract.en: Anything described this way is under pressure to become something else, and that pressure is what the word really names.
abstract.cn: 凡被这样形容的事物，都绷着一股要变成别的东西的力，这个词命名的其实就是这股力。

examples.en: The doctor told her she was pregnant with twins.
examples.cn: 医生告诉她怀的是双胞胎。

examples.en: He let a pregnant pause hang in the air before answering.
examples.cn: 他先让一阵意味深长的停顿悬在空中，然后才回答。

examples.en: The old harbour is pregnant with possibility.
examples.cn: 这座旧港口孕育着各种可能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来个男童」——家里即将扑来一个小男童；pregnant 就是怀孕的。

root: 源自拉丁语 praegnans（怀孕的），由 prae-（在前）与表示出生的词根 gen- 构成，词干 pregnant- 经古法语进入英语；同族词有 pregnancy、impregnate。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hidden life carried inside; the senses divide into the bodily state, meaning held back, stored possibility, and an old praise of a fertile mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是怀在里面的隐秘生命；义项由此分出身体状态、未尽的意思、储存的可能，以及对丰沛头脑的旧式赞美。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a woman resting one hand on her rounded belly and looking down at it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位妇人一手扶着腰，低头看向自己微微隆起的腹部。

branches.en: a hand resting on a rounded belly
branches.cn: 一只手扶着隆起的腹部

branches.en: a speaker stopping mid-sentence while the room waits
branches.cn: 说话人停在半句，满屋等着

branches.en: a seed under soil that has not broken through
branches.cn: 土下尚未破土的种子

branches.en: a notebook crowded with half-finished ideas
branches.cn: 写满未完成想法的笔记本

branches.en: an unfinished sentence that promises more
branches.cn: 一句没说完却暗示更多的话

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix of place plus a root of birth, and English built its nouns and verbs on the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀加上表示出生的词根构成，英语又在同一词干上造出名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Pregnant goes back to Latin praegnans and its stem pregnant-, built from prae- and a root for birth; Latin also used gravida for a pregnant woman.
latinIntro.cn: pregnant 上溯拉丁语 praegnans 及其词干 pregnant-，由 prae- 与表示出生的词根构成；拉丁语另用 gravida 指孕妇。

items.meaning: the stem used in inflected cases
the state of carrying a child
to make pregnant or to fill throughout

definition_zh: 偏见；成见；使有偏见；损害
definition_en: a preconceived opinion formed without adequate grounds, or to bias someone or to harm a right or interest
core_image: 一叠贴好标签的档案袋，还没打开就已经判定了内容
scene: 招聘会上，一名主管看到简历上的外地学校名称，就把材料放到一边。The trainer calls that reflex prejudice rather than a hiring rule.
sceneCN: 这里 prejudice 指「未经充分了解就形成的成见」（第 1 个义项：预先形成、缺乏依据的看法）；句意为培训师把那种反射式的反应称为偏见，而非招聘规则。场景要素：简历堆、标签、被推到一边的文件夹；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 偏见；成见；（法律）损害
使有偏见；损害（权利、机会）

collocations.zh: 不影响法律权利地；不损及权益

derivatives.zh: 由 prejudice 加过去分词词尾构成，指自己抱有偏见的
由 prejudice 加形容词后缀构成，指会造成损害的
由否定前缀加 prejudiced 构成，指不带偏见的
由表「在前」的前缀加 judge 构成，指事先就作出判断

senses.title: An opinion formed without adequate grounds
senses.definition: a judgment about someone or something made before the facts are known
senses.definitionCN: 在了解事实之前就对某人某物作出的判断
senses.example: Her prejudice about the neighbourhood faded after a single afternoon there.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那个街区的成见，在待了一个下午之后就淡了。
senses.why: The Latin noun means a judgment made beforehand, so the word records not hatred but the timing of the judgment.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁名词意为「事先作出的判断」，因此这个词记录的不是仇恨，而是判断的时点。

senses.title: Hostility toward a group
senses.definition: a hostile or unfair orientation toward people because of the group they belong to
senses.definitionCN: 因某人所属的群体而对其持有的敌意或不公取向
senses.example: The report documented prejudice against migrant workers in hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了招聘中对外来务工人员的偏见。
senses.why: A pre-judgment aimed at a whole category turns into hostility, and this is the sense most people mean today.
senses.whyCN: 针对整个类别的预先判断会变成敌意，这也是今天多数人所指的义项。

senses.title: A favourable pre-judgment
senses.definition: a pre-judgment that can lean in someone's favour as well as against them
senses.definitionCN: 一种可能有利于某人、也可能不利于某人的预先判断
senses.example: His prejudice in favour of old buildings made him miss the mould in the basement.
senses.exampleCN: 他对老房子的偏爱让他忽略了地下室的霉斑。
senses.why: English keeps the neutral frame, so the word can describe a favourable lean, which is why 'prejudice in favour of' still occurs.
senses.whyCN: 英语保留了中性框架，因此这个词可以形容有利的倾斜，「偏爱」的说法至今仍在用。

senses.title: To bias someone's mind
senses.titleCN: 使某人的判断带上偏向
senses.definition: to cause someone to form an opinion in advance of the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 使某人在证据出现之前就形成看法
senses.example: The leaked summary prejudiced the panel before it heard a witness.
senses.exampleCN: 提前流出的摘要让评审团在听证之前就有了倾向。
senses.why: The verb turns the state into an act: someone or something does the pre-judging to another mind.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个状态变成动作：某人或某物把预先判断做进了另一个头脑。

senses.title: To harm a right or interest
senses.definition: to damage or impair a legal right, a claim or a chance
senses.definitionCN: 损害或削弱某项法律权利、主张或机会
senses.example: The delay prejudiced the tenant's claim to compensation.
senses.exampleCN: 这拖延损害了租客获得补偿的主张。
senses.why: Law generalised the word from a wrong opinion to any action that puts a right at a disadvantage.
senses.whyCN: 法律把这个词从「错误的看法」推广到任何使权利处于不利地位的行为。

senses.title: A dismissal that bars refiling
senses.definition: in procedure, a final dismissal of a claim that prevents it being brought again
senses.definitionCN: 程序上对某项主张的终局驳回，使其不得再次提出
senses.example: The case was dismissed with prejudice after the plaintiff failed to appear.
senses.exampleCN: 原告未出庭后，案件以终局方式驳回。
senses.why: A final ruling 'prejudges' the matter for good, which is why the old word survives in this narrow procedural formula.
senses.whyCN: 终局裁决等于把这件事实地预先判定了，因此这个古老的词在这条狭窄的程序套语里留存。

senses.title: A social attitude distinct from behaviour
senses.titleCN: 与社会行为相区别的态度
senses.definition: in social psychology, an attitude toward a group, studied separately from discriminatory acts
senses.definitionCN: 社会心理学中，对某群体的态度，与歧视行为分开研究
senses.example: Prejudice and discrimination are measured as attitude and action, not as one thing.
senses.exampleCN: 偏见与歧视被分别测作态度与行为，而不是同一件事。
senses.why: The discipline needed to split the inner leaning from the outward act, so the word was fixed to the inner side.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科需要把内心的倾斜与外显的行为分开，于是把这个词固定在内心一侧。

senses.title: To the detriment of someone
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase, to the disadvantage or injury of a person or interest
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法中，指使某人或某种利益处于不利或受损
senses.example: The new route was chosen to the prejudice of the fishing village.
senses.exampleCN: 新路线被选中，代价是渔村受损。
senses.why: The prepositional phrase keeps the harm sense alive outside courtrooms, where it means damage in plain speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个介词短语把损害义留在法庭之外，日常言谈中它就指造成的损失。

intro.en: Prejudice comes through Old French from Latin praejudicium 'a judgment beforehand', built from a prefix meaning 'before' and the noun for judgment. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: prejudice 经古法语来自拉丁语 praejudicium「事先的判断」，由表「在前」的前缀与表「判断」的名词构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: The prefix meant 'before, in front', and it fixes the timing of the judgment in the word itself.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为「在前、在之前」，它把判断的时点固定在词里。

items.en: Judicium meant a declaring or a ruling, built on judex 'judge', itself from law plus the verb for declaring.
items.cn: judicium 意为宣告或裁断，建立在 judex「法官」之上，而后者又由「法律」与表「宣告」的动词构成。

items.en: The compound named a preliminary ruling and, in ordinary use, an opinion formed before the case was heard.
items.cn: 这个复合名词指初步裁决，在日常用法中也指在听取案件之前就形成的看法。

items.en: Old French prejudice carried both the legal and the mental senses into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把这个词的法律义与心智义一并带入英语。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word narrowed toward hostility between groups, and psychology later separated it from discrimination.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词向群体间的敌意收窄，心理学后来把它与歧视区分开。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the earliest English use is recorded only approximately, and the pre-Latin origin of the word for law is unsettled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：最早的英语用例只有约略记载；那个表「法律」的词在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words and adjectives that are routinely mixed up with the noun; group two holds near neighbours for a group-directed attitude.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词，以及常与本名词弄混的形容词；第二组是表示针对群体的态度的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes a person who holds a prejudice; the noun names the prejudice itself, and the two are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容人抱有偏见；名词指偏见本身，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: Means likely to cause damage to a right or a case; it does not mean full of prejudice.
entries.definitionCN: 意为很可能损害某项权利或案件，并不表示「充满偏见」。

entries.definition: A ruling or a formed opinion without the prefix, so it says nothing about whether the opinion came too early.
entries.definitionCN: 不带该前缀的裁决或看法，因此并不表明这个看法是否来得太早。

entries.tag: the verb built with the same prefix
entries.definition: To judge before hearing the evidence; it is the act that produces a prejudice.
entries.definitionCN: 指在听取证据之前就判断，正是产生偏见的行为。

entries.definition: Any leaning, often unconscious and sometimes harmless; prejudice implies an unfair or unfounded leaning.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何偏向，往往无意识且有时无害；prejudice 暗示不公或缺乏依据。

entries.definition: Treating people differently in practice; psychology keeps it separate from the inner attitude that prejudice names.
entries.definitionCN: 指实际行为上的区别对待；心理学把它与 prejudice 所指的内心的态度分开。

entries.definition: A simplified image of a group; a stereotype can supply the content of a prejudice but is not itself hostility.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某群体的简化形象；它可为偏见提供内容，但本身不是敌意。

entries.definition: Stubborn intolerance of another group, stronger and more openly hostile than prejudice.
entries.definitionCN: 指对另一群体的顽固不容忍，比 prejudice 更强、更公开敌意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real judging root, the real family and the real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、表「判断」的词根、真实的词族与真实的法律说法。

normal.en: The prefix means before and the base means judgment, so prejudice is a judgment that arrives before the facts.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「在前」，基底意为「判断」，因此偏见就是赶在事实之前到达的判断。

normal.en: The family runs judge, judgment, judicial, prejudice, prejudiced, prejudicial, prejudge.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 judge、judgment、judicial、prejudice、prejudiced、prejudicial、prejudge。

normal.en: Legal phrases preserve the harm sense: without prejudice, dismissed with prejudice, to the prejudice of.
normal.cn: 法律说法保存了损害义：不损及权益、以终局方式驳回、损害……的利益。

normal.en: The adjective prejudiced describes a person, while prejudicial describes something harmful.
normal.cn: 形容词 prejudiced 形容人，而 prejudicial 形容有害之物。

normal.en: Social psychology separates the attitude from the act, calling them prejudice and discrimination.
normal.cn: 社会心理学把态度与行为分开，分别称为偏见与歧视。

abstract.en: Picture a folder labelled before it has been opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一个还没打开就已经贴好标签的文件夹。

abstract.en: Picture a lens ground before the optician has measured the eye.
abstract.cn: 想象磨好的镜片，而验光师还没量过眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a gavel that falls before the witness is sworn.
abstract.cn: 想象法槌在证人宣誓之前就落下了。

examples.en: The campaign measured prejudice through questions about hiring and housing.
examples.cn: 这场运动通过招聘与住房方面的问题来测量偏见。

examples.en: Reading one bad review prejudiced him against the whole school of thought.
examples.cn: 读了一篇差评，就让他对整个学派有了成见。

examples.en: The ruling was issued without prejudice to either party's further claims.
examples.cn: 该裁定不损及双方后续的主张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pre 在前 + judge 判断」——还没看清就先判了，就是偏见

root: 拉丁 praejudicium「事先的判断」由意为「在前」的前缀加 judicium（裁断，出自 judex「法官」= jus「法律」+ dicere「宣告」）；jus 更深来源不确定。英语 prejudice。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one early judgment: a verdict is reached before the evidence arrives. It is read as an unfounded opinion, as hostility toward a group, as a favourable lean, as the act of biasing a mind, as harm to a right, as a final dismissal, as an attitude studied apart from behaviour, and as a plain phrase for damage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「提前的判断」展开：证据未到，裁决先落。它依次被读作缺乏依据的看法、对群体的敌意、有利的倾斜、使他人带上偏向的行为、对权利的损害、终局驳回、与行为分开研究的态度，以及日常说法中的损失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of folders already labelled before any is opened.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠档案袋还没打开，标签就已经贴好。

branches.en: THE PRE-JUDGMENT: an unfounded opinion and a favourable one share the same timing, which is the real subject of the word.
branches.cn: 预先的判断：缺乏依据的看法与有利的看法共享同一个时点，时点才是这个词真正的主题。

branches.en: FROM OPINION TO ENMITY: when the early judgment is aimed at a whole group, it hardens into hostility.
branches.cn: 从看法到敌意：当提前的判断对准整个群体，它就硬化为敌意。

branches.en: DOING IT TO A MIND: the verb marks the moment one person's lean is planted in another.
branches.cn: 做进别人脑中：动词标出某人的倾斜被栽进另一个人头脑的那一刻。

branches.en: HARM: legal impairment and the everyday phrase for damage both turn a wrong opinion into a lost right.
branches.cn: 损害：法律上的削弱与日常说到损失的说法，都把错误的看法变成失去的权利。

branches.en: FIXED IN PLACE: a dismissal that bars refiling and an attitude studied apart from action both keep the first judgment from moving.
branches.cn: 固定原位：不得再诉的驳回与与行为分开研究的态度，都让最初的判断无法移动。

intro.en: Prejudice is a Latin prefix plus the same judging noun that builds judge and judgment, so the whole legal family reads together.
intro.cn: prejudice 是一个拉丁前缀加那个构成 judge 与 judgment 的「判断」名词，因此整个法律词族可以一起读。

latinIntro.en: The judging noun gives judge, judgment, judicial and judicious; the prefix meaning 'before' gives predict, prevent and prepare.

senses.title: Coming before the main part
senses.definition: happening or existing before the main event or part
senses.definitionCN: 在主事件或主体之前发生或存在
senses.example: We held preliminary talks before the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 峰会前我们举行了预备性会谈。
senses.why: The Latin phrase prae limine means 'before the threshold'. A preliminary step is taken at the doorway, before anyone enters the main room.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁短语 prae limine 意为“在门槛之前”。初步步骤是在门口完成的，还没进正厅。

senses.title: Introductory and preparatory
senses.definition: serving to introduce or prepare for something fuller
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出或准备更完整的东西
senses.example: The report begins with a few preliminary remarks.
senses.exampleCN: 报告以几句引言开篇。
senses.why: A preliminary remark prepares the listener's mind the way a vestibule prepares a house: it is part of the building, yet not the room you came for.
senses.whyCN: 引言为听者的心智做准备，如同门厅为房屋做准备：它是建筑的一部分，却不是你要进的那个房间。

senses.title: An early round of a competition
senses.definition: a contest or stage that narrows the field before the final
senses.definitionCN: 在决赛前缩小参赛范围的比赛或阶段
senses.example: She finished first in the preliminary.
senses.exampleCN: 她在预赛中名列第一。
senses.why: Sport borrows the word for its sieve stages. The preliminary exists only to produce the final list, so it is judged by who advances rather than who wins.
senses.whyCN: 体育借这个词来指“筛选阶段”。预赛只为产生决赛名单，所以评判标准是谁晋级，而不是谁夺冠。

senses.title: A preparatory step or arrangement
senses.definition: one of the things done in advance to make a main event possible
senses.definitionCN: 为主要事件铺路而事先完成的事项
senses.example: The preliminaries took longer than the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 准备事项比仪式本身还久。
senses.why: In the plural, the word names the whole backstage: forms, fees, introductions. These steps are usually invisible once the main event begins.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式命名整个后台：表格、费用、介绍。主事件一开始，这些步骤通常就看不见了。

senses.title: Provisional, not final
senses.definition: of a result or finding, based on early evidence and open to change
senses.definitionCN: 结果或发现基于早期证据，仍可能变动
senses.example: Preliminary findings suggest the drug is safe.
senses.exampleCN: 初步结果显示这种药是安全的。
senses.why: Science uses preliminary to mark a claim's status: it is offered for scrutiny, not asserted as settled. The word protects the speaker from the finality of proof.
senses.whyCN: 科学用 preliminary 标记一个主张的地位：它供审视，而非断言已定。这个词保护说话者，使其不必承担“已证”的终局。

senses.title: A qualifying heat in sport
senses.definition: a race or match that decides who enters the main competition
senses.definitionCN: 决定谁进入主赛的预跑或预赛
senses.example: He ran a personal best in the preliminaries.
senses.exampleCN: 他在预赛中跑出个人最好成绩。
senses.why: The heat is a filter, not a show. Preliminary times only select; medals are awarded later, which is why records set in heats can feel strangely weightless.
senses.whyCN: 预赛是筛子，不是演出。预赛成绩只作选拔；奖牌在后面发，所以预赛里创的纪录会有一种奇特的失重感。

senses.title: A hearing held before trial
senses.definition: a court session that decides whether a case should go to trial
senses.definitionCN: 决定案件是否进入正式审判的法庭程序
senses.example: The judge set a preliminary hearing for next month.
senses.exampleCN: 法官把预审定在下个月。
senses.why: Law needs a gate before the trial: the preliminary hearing tests whether there is enough evidence. The threshold image becomes a procedural safeguard.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要审判前的一道门：预审检验证据是否足够。门槛意象变成程序保障。

senses.title: An introductory statement or section
senses.definition: a short opening text that prepares the reader
senses.definitionCN: 为读者做准备的简短开篇文字
senses.example: The book opens with a preliminary on method.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书以一篇方法引言开篇。
senses.why: In scholarship, preliminaries include prefaces and front matter. They frame the main text the way a prologue frames a play: outside the action, yet necessary to it.
senses.whyCN: 在学术写作中，preliminaries 包括序言与卷首材料。它们框住正文，如同开场白框住戏剧：在情节之外，却不可或缺。

intro.en: Preliminary is a threshold word. Its Latin source is the phrase prae limine, 'before the threshold', and every sense keeps that image: something done at the door before entering.
intro.cn: preliminary 是一个关于门槛的词。它的拉丁来源是短语 prae limine“在门槛之前”，每个义项都保留这个意象：进门之前先在门口完成的事。

items.en: First recorded as an adjective meaning 'introductory, preparatory'.
items.cn: 最早记录为形容词，义为“引言的、预备的”。

items.en: From Latin prae limine 'before the threshold', from prae- 'before' and limen 'threshold, door'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁短语 prae limine“在门槛之前”，由 prae-“在前”与 limen“门槛、门”构成。

items.en: limen is the same noun behind eliminate and subliminal. A threshold is both a physical edge and the limit of what can be perceived.
items.cn: limen 也是 eliminate 与 subliminal 背后的名词。门槛既是物理边缘，也是感知的界限。

items.en: The noun use for preparatory steps and early rounds develops in the 18c.–19c., often in the plural.
items.cn: 指预备步骤与早期轮次的名词用法在 18–19 世纪发展起来，常用复数。

items.en: Modern English uses the adjective for provisional findings and the noun for sporting and legal gates.
items.cn: 现代英语用形容词指暂定结论，用名词指体育与法律中的“关口”。

note.en: The first group shares the limen or preliminary stem; the second is about words that also mean coming first or preparing the way.
note.cn: 第一组共享 limen 词干或 preliminary 的构词，第二组看同样表示“在先”或“铺路”的词。

entries.definition: a preliminary exam or round, used informally. It is a clipped form.
entries.definitionCN: 预考或预赛，非正式缩略。

entries.definition: preliminary exams or front matter in a book.
entries.definitionCN: 初试；书籍卷首材料。

entries.definition: below the threshold of consciousness. It uses the same Latin limen.
entries.definitionCN: 阈下的；意识界限以下的。它用同一个拉丁词 limen。

entries.definition: serving as an introduction. It names the function, not the threshold image.
entries.definitionCN: 用作引言的。它命名功能，而非门槛意象。

entries.definition: arranged for the present and liable to change. It fits preliminary findings but not early rounds.
entries.definitionCN: 暂时安排、可变的。它贴合“初步结果”，不贴合“预赛”。

entries.definition: done to get ready for something. It stresses readiness rather than position.
entries.definitionCN: 为某事做准备的。它强调准备状态，而非位置。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin limen 'threshold', the phrase prae limine, the sporting and legal gate uses, and the adjective/noun pair.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 limen“门槛”、短语 prae limine、体育与法律中的“关口”用法，以及形容词与名词两种词性。

normal.en: Prae limine means 'before the threshold'. Everything preliminary happens at the door, before the main room.
normal.cn: prae limine 意为“在门槛之前”。一切 preliminary 的事都发生在门口，还没进正厅。

normal.en: Limen is also in eliminate and subliminal: a threshold can be a physical edge or a limit of perception.
normal.cn: limen 也见于 eliminate 与 subliminal：门槛可以是物理边缘，也可以是感知界限。

normal.en: A preliminary round is a sieve: it exists to produce the final list, not to award the prize.
normal.cn: 预赛是一张筛子：它的存在是为了产生决赛名单，而不是发奖。

normal.en: Preliminary findings are offered for scrutiny, not asserted as settled. The word marks a claim as open.
normal.cn: 初步结果供审视，而非断言已定。这个词把主张标记为“未关”。

normal.en: The noun usually appears in the plural: the preliminaries are the backstage steps nobody watches.
normal.cn: 名词通常用复数：preliminaries 是没人观看的后台步骤。

abstract.en: Every entrance has a threshold, and every threshold has a rule: what must be left outside before you may come in.
abstract.cn: 每道入口都有门槛，每道门槛都有规则：进门之前必须把什么留在外面。

abstract.en: The preliminary is powerful because it decides who gets to be judged at all.
abstract.cn: 预赛之所以有力，是因为它决定谁才有资格被评判。

abstract.en: Calling a result preliminary is an act of intellectual honesty: it keeps the door open instead of sealing the room.
abstract.cn: 把结果称作“初步”，是一种智识上的诚实：它让门继续开着，而不是封死房间。

examples.en: The preliminary results look promising.
examples.cn: 初步结果看起来有希望。

examples.en: She was eliminated in the preliminary round.
examples.cn: 她在预赛轮被淘汰。

examples.en: These talks are preliminary to a formal agreement.
examples.cn: 这些会谈是正式协议的前奏。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of preliminary, all set at the threshold. The word can describe a step (talks, remarks), a stage (a heat, a hearing), or a status (findings still open to change).
sensesIntro.cn: preliminary 的八个义项都发生在门槛处。这个词可以描述一个步骤（会谈、引言）、一个阶段（预赛、预审），或一种状态（仍可变动的研究结果）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing at the threshold before entering the main room.
core.cn: 核心意象：进入正厅之前，站在门槛上。

branches.en: THRESHOLD: remarks and front matter stand outside the main text yet belong to it.
branches.cn: 门槛：引言与卷首材料站在正文之外，却属于它。

branches.en: PREPARE: the backstage steps make the main event possible.
branches.cn: 准备：后台步骤使主事件成为可能。

branches.en: QUALIFY: an early round filters the field before the final.
branches.cn: 选拔：早期轮次在决赛前筛出参赛者。

branches.en: PROVISIONAL: a finding marked preliminary is still open to revision.
branches.cn: 暂定：标记为初步的结论仍可修改。

branches.en: LEGAL GATE: a hearing tests whether a case may enter trial.
branches.cn: 法律关口：预审检验案件能否进入审判。

intro.en: Preliminary is an adjective that also works as a noun. English adds -ly and clips it to prelim, while the Latin limen also builds eliminate and subliminal.
intro.cn: preliminary 是可作名词的形容词。英语加 -ly，并缩略为 prelim；拉丁语 limen 还构成 eliminate 与 subliminal。

latinIntro.en: The Latin phrase prae limine 'before the threshold' yields preliminary and, through limen, eliminate and subliminal. The threshold is both a doorway and a limit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁短语 prae limine“在门槛之前”生成 preliminary，并经 limen 生成 eliminate 与 subliminal。门槛既是门口，也是界限。

definition_zh: 前提；前提假设；（复数）房屋及场地；法律文书开头陈述的事实；以……为前提预先提出
definition_en: a statement accepted as true and used as the basis of an argument, or (in the plural) a building and its land
core_image: 长桌的四条桌腿先稳稳立住，桌面上才摆得下一层层叠起的论证卡片
scene: 辩论开始前，主持人提醒双方先确认共同接受的基本判断，否则后面的推论都无处落脚。The whole argument rests on a premise that nobody has tested.
sceneCN: 这里指论证所依据的基本判断（第 1 个义项：作为论证基础的前提命题）；句意为整个论证都建立在一个无人检验过的前提上；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 前提；前提假设；（复数）房屋及场地
以……为前提预先提出（较少用）

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「房屋及场地；营业场所」
由动词加已然词尾构成，义为「以……为基础的」
逻辑学中的另一种拼写，义同「前提」
由「前提」与「基于」复合而成，义为「以前提为基础的」

senses.title: A proposition that supports an argument
senses.definition: a statement put forward as true so that a conclusion can be drawn from it
senses.definitionCN: 作为真实陈述提出、以便从中推出结论的命题
senses.example: The main premise of the essay is that prices reflect information.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章的主要前提是价格反映信息。
senses.why: The Latin word meant something sent before, and this sense places the statement ahead of the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词本义是「事先送出之物」，这一义项把它放在结论之前。

senses.title: An assumption taken without proof
senses.titleCN: 未加证明就接受的假设
senses.definition: a belief that a study or person accepts as true without testing it
senses.definitionCN: 研究或个人未经检验就当作真实的信念
senses.example: The model works only if its premise about human rationality holds.
senses.exampleCN: 只有当模型关于人类理性的假设成立时，它才有效。
senses.why: What is put before an argument is often simply granted, which is how a premise becomes an assumption.
senses.whyCN: 放在论证之前的东西常被直接认可，「前提」由此变成「假设」。

senses.title: The major premise of a syllogism
senses.definition: the general statement from which a syllogism begins, before the minor premise is applied
senses.definitionCN: 三段论起始的一般性陈述，在其后接上小前提
senses.example: The major premise says all mammals are warm-blooded.
senses.exampleCN: 大前提说所有哺乳动物都是温血的。
senses.why: Logic gave the word a fixed slot: the general claim sits first, and the specific case is placed under it.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学给这个词一个固定位置：一般性主张坐第一，具体事例被置于其下。

senses.title: The minor premise of a syllogism
senses.definition: the specific statement that brings a particular case under the general one
senses.definitionCN: 把具体事例归入一般陈述之下的特定陈述
senses.example: The minor premise states that this animal is a mammal.
senses.exampleCN: 小前提陈述这只动物是哺乳动物。
senses.why: The second slot in the syllogism is also called a premise, since both statements must be granted before the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 三段论中的第二个位置同样称为前提，因为两个陈述都必须先被认可，结论才成立。

senses.title: A building and its land
senses.definition: the buildings and the ground belonging to a business or an owner, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 属于某企业或业主的建筑物与土地，用复数形式
senses.example: The inspectors walked through the factory premises.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员走遍了工厂的场地。
senses.why: Legal deeds opened by describing the property set before the reader, and that list of property became the buildings themselves.
senses.whyCN: 法律契约开头先描述摆在读者面前的财产，这份财产清单后来就指建筑物本身。

senses.title: The property recited in a deed
senses.titleCN: 法律文书开头陈述的财产
senses.definition: the opening part of a legal instrument that sets out the facts and property concerned
senses.definitionCN: 法律文书开头说明相关事实与财产的部分
senses.example: The lease recites the premises before stating the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 这份租约在说明租金之前先陈述标的财产。
senses.why: The word names what is placed in front of the operative clauses, so it labels that opening recital.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指放在操作性条款之前的内容，因此用来指开头的陈述部分。

senses.title: A condition treated as given
senses.titleCN: 模型中当作给定的条件
senses.definition: a condition that a model or calculation accepts as fixed before it begins
senses.definitionCN: 模型或计算在开始之前就当作固定条件的设定
senses.example: The estimate rests on the premise that fuel prices stay flat.
senses.exampleCN: 这一估算建立在燃料价格持平的假设之上。
senses.why: A model must fix something before it can move, and whatever is fixed is literally placed in front.
senses.whyCN: 模型必须先固定某些东西才能运转，被固定者正被摆在最前面。

senses.title: A claim a debate must grant
senses.titleCN: 辩论中须先接受的主张
senses.definition: a statement that one side asks the other to accept before the exchange can proceed
senses.definitionCN: 一方要求另一方在交锋开始前先接受的主张
senses.example: The judge asked whether both sides shared that premise.
senses.exampleCN: 主持人问双方是否共有那个前提。
senses.why: Debate is an argument built in public, so it needs a floor of agreed statements under it.
senses.whyCN: 辩论是当众搭建的论证，因此需要一层公认陈述作地板。

senses.title: To state something beforehand
senses.definition: to set something out in advance as a basis for what follows
senses.definitionCN: 事先把某内容摆出来，作为后续论述的基础
senses.example: Let me premise my answer with one condition.
senses.exampleCN: 请允许我先以一个条件作为回答的前提。
senses.why: The verb kept the Latin sense of sending something ahead, and English uses it rarely, mostly in formal prose.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语「事先送出」的意思，英语中很少用，多见于正式书面语。

intro.en: Premise comes from Latin praemissa, things sent before, from praemittere, to send ahead. Logic took the word for the statements placed before a conclusion, and law took it for the property described at the start of a deed; the plural then became the buildings themselves.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 praemissa「事先送出之物」，出自动词「预先送出」。逻辑学用它指放在结论之前的陈述，法律用它指契约开头描述的财产，其复数随后就指建筑物本身。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or let go, and it stands behind words of sending, such as mission and transmit.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「送、放出」，英语中表示发送的词多出自它。

items.en: The prefix prae- added «in front», so the verb meant to send something ahead of what follows.
items.cn: 前缀加上「在前」，于是动词意为把某物先于后续内容送出去。

items.en: The neuter plural named the things set before a conclusion, and logic adopted it as a technical term.
items.cn: 中性复数指放在结论之前的内容，逻辑学把它采用为术语。

items.en: Translations of Aristotle fixed major and minor premise as the two statements above and below the conclusion.
items.cn: 对亚里士多德著作的翻译固定了「大前提」与「小前提」，即结论之上与之下的两个陈述。

items.en: Deeds opened by reciting the property, and the plural premises came to mean that property and then the buildings on it.
items.cn: 契约开头先陈述财产，复数形式便指该财产，随后又指其上的建筑物。

items.en: The building sense now lives almost entirely in the plural, while the logic sense keeps the singular; the split's exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 建筑物义如今几乎只存在于复数，逻辑义则保留单数；两者分开的确切年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the same Latin root or looks close; the second group names other starting points of reasoning.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一拉丁词根或形近；第二组指推理的其他起点。

entries.definition: The plural noun for a building and its land, from the property clause of a deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指房屋及场地，来自契约中的财产条款。

entries.definition: Based on a stated assumption; the past participle used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指以某陈述假设为基础的，是过去分词作形容词。

entries.definition: The older spelling used in logic for a stated proposition.
entries.definitionCN: 逻辑学中指前提命题的旧拼写。

entries.definition: First in rank; it belongs to the Latin word for first, not to sending ahead.
entries.definitionCN: 指地位最高的；属于拉丁语「第一」，与「预先送出」无关。

entries.definition: A bonus or an insurance payment; it comes from the word for reward.
entries.definitionCN: 指奖金或保险费；来自表示报酬的词。

entries.definition: A declaration that one will do something; its root is to send forth a word, a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指表示将做某事的声明；其词根是「送出话语」，属另一动词。

entries.definition: Something accepted as true without evidence, often silently.
entries.definitionCN: 指无证据而被接受为真的东西，常是默许的。

entries.definition: A belief that must already hold for a statement to make sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个陈述要成立就必须先已存在的信念。

entries.definition: A statement that can be judged true or false.
entries.definitionCN: 指可判断真假的陈述。

entries.definition: A tentative explanation offered for testing, not merely granted.
entries.definitionCN: 指提出来供检验的暂时解释，而不只是被认可。

entries.definition: A principle accepted without proof as a starting point.
entries.definitionCN: 指无需证明即被接受作为出发点的原理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the table-leg picture, the syllogism slots, the legal deed and the everyday plural.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用桌腿画面、三段论的两个位置、法律契约与日常复数用法。

normal.en: A premise is sent before the conclusion, just as a table leg is placed before the table top.
normal.cn: 前提先于结论送出，正如桌腿先于桌面立好。

normal.en: The major premise is the wide statement; the minor premise puts one case under it.
normal.cn: 大前提是宽的一般陈述，小前提把一个事例放到它下面。

normal.en: Premises in the plural are buildings, from the property clause at the head of a deed.
normal.cn: 复数形式指建筑物，来自契约开头的财产条款。

normal.en: A false premise makes a valid argument reach a wrong conclusion.
normal.cn: 前提错了，形式有效的论证也会得出错误结论。

normal.en: On the premise that is the everyday phrase that carries the logic sense into ordinary writing.
normal.cn: 「以……为前提」是把逻辑义带入日常写作的固定说法。

abstract.en: A premise is a floor that nobody looks at until the argument falls through it.
abstract.cn: 前提是一块地板，直到论证掉了下去，才有人低头看它。

abstract.en: Every model stands on statements it never proves, and that silence is what makes it usable.
abstract.cn: 每个模型都站在它从不证明的陈述上，正是这份沉默让它可用。

abstract.en: The same word can name a sentence and a building, because both are things set in front of you.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指一句话，也能指一栋楼，因为两者都是摆在你面前的东西。

examples.en: The study rests on the premise that memory declines with age.
examples.cn: 这项研究建立在记忆随年龄衰退这一前提上。

examples.en: If the premise is false, the conclusion cannot stand.
examples.cn: 如果前提错误，结论就站不住。

examples.en: Visitors must not smoke anywhere on the premises.
examples.cn: 访客不得在场地内任何地方吸烟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普瑞密斯」——「普」通人先「密」密接受的那句话，就是推理的前提

root: 拉丁语 praemissa「事先送出之物」← praemittere「预先送出」= prae-「在前」+ mittere「送、放」。逻辑学经中世纪翻译固定「大前提、小前提」，法律契约开头的财产陈述引申出「房屋及场地」。十五世纪起见于英语；两义分化的确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from logic to property: a supporting proposition, an untested assumption, the major and minor premises, buildings and land, a deed recital, a fixed model condition, a debated claim, and the rare verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从逻辑延伸到财产：支撑命题、未验证假设、大前提、小前提、房屋场地、契约陈述、模型条件、辩论主张，以及少用的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four legs are set down first, and only then can the stacked cards of argument rest on the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：先放下四条桌腿，论证的卡片堆才放得上桌面。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT FLOOR: the proposition that must be granted before debate can proceed.
branches.cn: 论证的地板：辩论开始前必须先被认可的那个命题。

branches.en: THE UNPROVED GRANT: assumptions that a person or a model simply accepts.
branches.cn: 未经证明的认可：人或模型直接接受的假设。

branches.en: THE TWO LOGIC SLOTS: the general statement and the case placed under it.
branches.cn: 逻辑的两个位置：一般陈述与置于其下的事例。

branches.en: THE LEGAL PROPERTY: the recited property and the buildings standing on it.
branches.cn: 法律上的财产：契约陈述的财产及其上的建筑物。

branches.en: THE RARE VERB: to send a condition ahead as a basis.
branches.cn: 少用的动词义：事先把一个条件送出作为基础。

intro.en: Premise is a Latin participle turned noun, and the same root that sends things ahead also produced words of mission and transmission.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语分词转成的名词，同一个「预先送出」词根也产生了「使命」「传送」等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies praemittere and praemissa; the logic and property senses both grew from the idea of things placed in front.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「预先送出」与「事先送出之物」；逻辑义与财产义都从「摆在前面之物」长出来。

items.exampleCN: 它标出事先送出的东西。

items.example: The root of mission and transmit.
items.exampleCN: 这是「使命」与「传送」的词根。

items.example: The direct source of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这是该名词的直接来源。

items.example: It became the logic term for a premise.
It marks the rare English verb premise.
items.exampleCN: 它标明这个少用的英语动词。

items.example: The legal sense moved into everyday property talk.
items.exampleCN: 法律义进入日常财产用语。

items.meaning: a statement set before a conclusion
items.example: The everyday singular that carries the logic sense.
items.exampleCN: 这是承载逻辑义的日常单数形式。

items.example: It survives chiefly in British academic prose.
items.exampleCN: 它主要保留在英国学术写作中。

definition_zh: 准备；预备；配制品；（复数）筹备工作
definition_en: the act of making something or someone ready, or a substance made ready for a particular use
core_image: 厨房案板上一排切好的食材、一张写满步骤的纸，锅还没上火
scene: 这场考试的准备工作比考试本身花的时间还长。Preparation for the exam took longer than the exam itself.
sceneCN: 这里 preparation 是「准备工作、预备」（第 1 个义项：使事情就绪的过程）；句意：备考所花的时间比考试本身还长。图中可辨识物件：切好的食材、步骤纸、尚未点火的锅；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 准备；预备；配制品；筹备工作
